item.title: What impressed LeBron James most about 76ers’ Tyrese Maxey in win vs. Knicks
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images What impressed LeBron James most about 76ers’ Tyrese Maxey in win vs. Knicks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . NEW YORK — After All-Star LeBron James made his Philadelphia 76ers debut in a 106-100 win against the New York Knicks, he shared what impressed him most about Tyrese Maxey, who tallied a game-high 28 points. Joel Embiid told Maxey he felt something different about the 76ers’ approach against the Knicks, a division rival. Philadelphia spoiled New York’s first championship banner night in 53 years on Tuesday. After the win, James revealed what stood out most about Maxey’s impressive performance. “His stamina. It seems like he doesn’t get tired,” James said. “He’s one of the fastest guys in the league. If not the fastest, with or without the ball.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “His stamina. It seems like he doesn’t get tired. He’s one of the fastest guys in the league. If not, the fastest, with or without the ball” LeBron James on what’s impressed him the most about Tyrese Maxey in the 76ers’ win against the Knicks pic.twitter.com/quFBhrfWH3 — Josue Pavón (@Joe_Sway) October 21, 2026 76ers’ Tyrese Maxey went 9-of-19 attempts from the floor, including a pair of threes, and 8-for-9 from the free-throw line. He also finished with five assists, four rebounds, three steals, and three blocks. LeBron James added 14 points, nine rebounds, seven assists, one steals, and one block in his 76ers debut at Madison Square Garden. Although the 76ers kicked off the 2026-27 regular season 1-0, James understands there’s still 81 games left. Still, it’s a step in the right direction for a Sixers team that added nine players to its roster over the summer. “It’s one game. Obviously, we can lear from the good things that we did. We can learn from the bad things we did tonight,” James said after Tuesday’s win. “I thought in the fourth quarter we did a good job of executing. We did a good job of pressing the tempo when we got the lead. And then, when they cut the lead, they made some timely shots. “Obviously, Tyrese was Tyrese. When you look at the three on the right wing from Joel, when you look at the three from KCP right by their bench at the end of the clock, and some of the plays that JB and JV had was special, too. Big shoutout to Ant [Anfernee Simons], too. Those minutes he gave us really was crucial. With second leg of the 76ers’ first back-to-back of the season on deck, the Sixers won’t have time to celebrate much before hosting the Cleveland Cavs on Wednesday. Related: Tyrese Maxey keeps it real about Kentavious Caldwell-Pope after 76ers win vs. Knicks Related: 76ers’ Joel Embiid issues strong defensive declaration in locker room after beating Knicks

item.title: Expanded Dylan Larkin trade list provides Red Wings’ Shawn Horcoff his biggest challenge
item.description: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Expanded Dylan Larkin trade list provides Red Wings’ Shawn Horcoff his biggest challenge appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin requested a trade from the team in the summer. After 10 years without playoff hockey, Larkin had seemingly lost faith in the team’s rebuilding process. He wanted a fresh start, and more importantly, a chance to contend for a Stanley Cup. His trade request is ongoing and unfulfilled to this point . Larkin is still with the Red Wings, providing value on the ice. For instance, he was the primary assist on Alex DeBrincat’s game-tying goal late in a loss to the Seattle Kraken on Tuesday night. However, that game is not the central story regarding Larkin at this time. The big news of the day is something Detroit fans have wanted to see happen for a while. The former captain has reportedly expanded his trade list to 10 teams, adding about six or seven teams to his previously short list. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This is a massive development for the Red Wings. More specifically, interim general manager Shawn Horcoff has more room to work with. At the same time, though, he has his biggest challenge still ahead of him. Expanded Dylan Larkin list doesn’t mean a trade is easy © Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images The 10 teams that Larkin would accept a trade to are as follows: the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. This was first reported by Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press on Tuesday. Some of these teams have been known for some time. Some of those same teams are also non-starters for the Red Wings. The Panthers, for instance, don’t have the assets needed to make this work. The Wild have some intriguing pieces, but still aren’t quite there in terms of value. Part of the reason Larkin wasn’t traded before the season was due to the short list. Outside of the two mentioned teams, the Golden Knights and the Stars were also rumored to be in play. Dallas had the young talent to make it work, but weren’t willing to part with it to get him. Vegas is in a similar boat to Florida. Having more teams to work with certainly gives Horcoff a better chance to make a deal that works for everyone. At the same time, this is a complicated situation. Having more teams to trade with doesn’t solve all of his problems. There are certainly teams on here that stand out. The Hurricanes have a lot of young talent that could be intriguing. The Mammoth, Devils, and Capitals are also intriguing fits. Even the Lightning could work. However, the incentive still lacks for many of these teams. Carolina just won the Stanley Cup and doesn’t need Larkin. Utah traded for Vincent Trocheck in the summer when it seemed Larkin wasn’t open to going there. New Jersey is pretty well

Carolina just won the Stanley Cup and doesn’t need Larkin. Utah traded for Vincent Trocheck in the summer when it seemed Larkin wasn’t open to going there. item.title: Foden says he’s finding his best form after stunning Champions League hat-trick
item.description: Foden says he’s finding his best form after stunning Champions League hat-trick Phil Foden believes he is getting back to his best after scoring a hat-trick in Manchester City 's 5-1 thrashing of AEK Athens in the Champions League . Foden produced a clinical performance as Enzo Maresca's side continued their good form with an emphatic Etihad win. The 26-year-old's sharp touch and finish doubled City's lead after Elliot Anderson's opener, before Rayan Cherki made it three, after the visitors had briefly threatened a comeback. A fabulous second from Foden extended the advantage further, before the midfielder tapped in from close range to seal the match ball. Foden's return to goalscoring form was a welcome sight for City, who started without Erling Haaland. Antoine Semenyo's two-month absence also leaves the Cityzens light at centre-forward, with Foden closing out the game in a false nine role. It's a position he says he enjoys, after a standout showing in the Champions League. “I enjoyed that a lot,” Foden said, via mancity.com. “The lads were great again. We showed determination again, it wasn’t pretty at times. We were giving sloppy passes away. “But, we stuck at the game plan and we kept going and in the end we broke them down. Overall I’m delighted. [My favourite goal is] probably the second to be honest. The way it went in. “I’m delighted to score goals now, I’m a forward so I have to keep scoring and helping the team. It’ll only do good for my confidence. “Slowly but surely [getting back to my best], still got a long way to go. I’m going in the right direction. Scoring along the way definitely helps. "I’ve just got to keep working hard and try to be as best as I can for the manager and for the team. Especially when I changed into the false 9 role, I really enjoyed it a lot. In between the lines and in the pockets where I like to be and linking the play. I really enjoyed that role tonight.”

item.title: 'Lucky and blessed' - Charles Barkley makes feelings clear on ability to 'steal money'
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images Charles Barkley has been one of the biggest names in basketball for a long time, and he has now opened up about the fortunate position he is in. The 63-year-old, who is a former MVP and an 11-time All-Star, retired from the sport in 2000, and since then, he has been a popular analyst on television. Barkley loves what he does, but has now claimed that he feels like he’s stealing money by being a pundit on TV. Charles Barkley admits he is lucky to have his broadcasting career Barkley could’ve put his feet up and relaxed after his retirement in 2000, but he jumped into punditry almost immediately. The veteran has been analysing games and giving his thoughts for over 25 years now, and he has reflected on that journey with a lot of gratitude. Barkley has called his ability to play basketball a gift, but he feels earning a handsome living by speaking about the game he loves is like ‘stealing money’. On The Association on NBA’s official channels, Barkley sat down to talk about the new season before opening up humbly about his broadcasting career. He said: “Man, just how lucky I am to do something (like this). Like, I tell people all the time, we are the luckiest people in the world. We get to do something stupid like play basketball and talk about it. “We’re not teachers, we’re not firemen, we’re not policemen, we’re not nurses, we’re not anybody in the armed service. To be able to play basketball, which is, like hitting a lottery, and then steal money on television talking about it, I’m just grateful and thankful. “Because you think about that: I get paid to watch LeBron James, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum. Number one, to get to play was a gift, but now to steal money talking about it on television, and I just feel so lucky and blessed and grateful. “Coming from a small town in Alabama, a couple thousand people, and look at my life 63 years later. I’m just grateful and thankful. That’s all I am. I mean that sincerely, not trying to be humble. “Like I say, we’re not teachers, we’re not firemen or policemen, but to be able to play basketball is a great gift, but to be able to just go on there for the last all these dozens of years and be able to talk about it, I’m just grateful and thankful.” In a world full of huge egos, seeing a Hall of Famer who has been at the very top as a player and a broadcaster be this humble is a breath of fresh air and genuinely fantastic to see. item.title: Man City owners forced to sell?! Watchdog chair confirms 'ABSOLUTE power' to oust Sheikh Mansour after financial breaches
item.description: Sheikh Mansour Manchester City - Getty Images Financial breaches spark regulatory scrutiny An independent commission recently concluded that Manchester City bypassed Premier League regulations over a nine-season period . According to the verdict, City established artificial commercial deals, inflating revenue and cutting costs by more than £900 million. The Etihad outfit was also found to have made concerted efforts to obstruct the Premier League's investigation into these financial arrangements. While City have officially appealed the initial ruling , the prospect of unprecedented sanctions now hangs over the Citizens. IFR chair asserts 'absolute power' over owners IFR chair asserts 'absolute power' over owners Speaking on The Rest Is Football podcast, IFR chair David Kogan clarified the extent of the regulator's authority. While stressing that it remains too early to determine specific actions while City's appeal is ongoing, he confirmed the organisation's ability to oust Sheikh Mansour. "We have the power to ask an owner to step away from a club if we believe that they run a club in a way that is neither fit, fair, or done with propriety," Kogan explained. When pressed on whether an ownership group could simply refuse to sell, he delivered a definitive response: "No, no, no. We've got absolute power to do so." Kogan also addressed the possibility of the IFR launching its own inquiry into the club's conduct. "I am not going to get pushed into making any judgement on this until we've seen all of those questions being answered," he said. "Then we will have to decide whether we're going to mount our own investigation and come to a conclusion on that and what we're going to do. And pre-empting that would be a colossal mistake." Diplomatic tensions and unprecedented penalties The current charges represent an existential threat to the club's era of dominance, with potential punishments ranging from massive fines to outright expulsion from the top tier. Reports suggest one scenario involves a "double relegation" threat , which would strip away the advantages gained during the alleged breaches and force a complete structural rebuild by trapping the club in the Championship for a minimum of two years. Beyond the pitch, the situation threatens to evolve into a significant diplomatic issue between the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates. Acknowledging these political sensitivities, Kogan has previously promised to resign if he experiences any governmental interference during a potential IFR investigation. Anxious wait for the appeal verdict Anxious wait for the appeal verdict Manchester City will continue to contest the findings aggressively, claiming to hold "irrefutable evidence" of their innocence. Meanwhile, the Premier League is allegedly eager to finalise and announce disciplinary measures before the club's appeal process concludes. The football world now waits to see if the Etihad club will face the ultimate sporting penalty.

item.title: Jamie Carragher has noticed one trend which ‘bodes well’ for Liverpool under Andoni Iraola
item.description: Jamie Carragher has noticed one trend which ‘bodes well’ for Liverpool under Andoni Iraola Jamie Carragher has noticed one trait under Andoni Iraola which ‘bodes well’ for Liverpool going forward, even if he feels there is ‘something still missing’ from the Reds. The Basque was in danger of suffering a second successive home defeat on Tuesday night when his team were 0-2 down to Villarreal after half an hour, but they recovered to win 4-3, opening a two-goal lead before the visitors struck again late on. It’s already the fifth time in 11 games this season in which LFC have come from behind to either win or draw, having salvage a late point against both Newcastle and Nottingham Forest and completed comebacks to beat Atletico Madrid, Brentford and now Villarreal. Carragher praises Liverpool’s resilience That’s already once more than they managed in the whole of 2025/26 under Arne Slot, and while Carragher is pleased at Liverpool’s resilience, he’s still waiting for an ‘outstanding performance’ since Iraola took charge in the summer. On Tuesday’s win over Villarreal, the pundit said on CBS Sports Golazo (via liverpool.com ): “Typical Liverpool all season, really, where there still hasn’t been one outstanding performance where you feel like the attack’s flowed and they’ve been strong defensively. They’ve had times where defensively they’ve looked strong but struggled to score. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) “The last couple of outings in the Champions League have been lots of goals, so they’re still searching for an almost top performance, really; but what they have done under Iraola so far is they’ve had an ability to come back from behind. They’ve done that a lot. They didn’t do that a lot last season at all. “They’ve done it again tonight, so that bodes well character-wise, but there’s still something short, something still missing, really, I would say, so far.” Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Encouraging to see, but not what you want too often Liverpool’s ability to come from behind to either win or draw is an encouraging trend which shows a new-found resilience that was sorely lacking last season, although they must be careful not to find themselves in a losing position too often. They deserve credit for battling back from 2-0 down to win last night, but if they were to find themselves in a similar hole against Brighton or Arsenal over the next fortnight, it’d be hard to see them pulling off another comeback. As Carragher says, the Reds have tended to be either free-scoring but brittle defensively (6-3 v LASK, 4-3 v Villarreal, 2-2 v Newcastle and Forest), or resilient at the back but impotent up top (0-0 v Fulham, 1-0 v Bournemouth). It’s a balance that Iraola is yet to fully get right, but at least Liverpool fans needn’t fear the worst if their team were to fall behind, knowing that they’ve proven their ability to fight back and salvage either one

(Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) “The last couple of outings in the Champions League have been lots of goals, so they’re still searching for an almost top performance, really; but what they have done under Iraola so far is they’ve had an ability to come back from behind. They’ve done that a lot. They didn’t do that a lot last season at all. “They’ve done it again tonight, so that bodes well character-wise, but there’s still something short, something still missing, really, I would say, so far.” Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Encouraging to see, but not what you want too often Liverpool’s ability to come from behind to either win or draw is an encouraging trend which shows a new-found resilience that was sorely lacking last season, although they must be careful not to find themselves in a losing position too often. They deserve credit for battling back from 2-0 down to win last night, but if they were to find themselves in a similar hole against Brighton or Arsenal over the next fortnight, it’d be hard to see them pulling off another comeback. As Carragher says, the Reds have tended to be either free-scoring but brittle defensively (6-3 v LASK, 4-3 v Villarreal, 2-2 v Newcastle and Forest), or resilient at the back but impotent up top (0-0 v Fulham, 1-0 v Bournemouth). It’s a balance that Iraola is yet to fully get right, but at least Liverpool fans needn’t fear the worst if their team were to fall behind, knowing that they’ve proven their ability to fight back and salvage either one point or three. It’s good to know that quality is there, but let’s hope the Reds don’t have to exhibit it too many more times over the course of the season!

item.title: FEATURE | The Bundesliga’s best 5 players – Matchday 6
item.description: FEATURE | The Bundesliga’s best 5 players – Matchday 6 Bundesliga Matchday 6 produced another entertaining weekend of German football, with Bayern Munich’s emphatic 6-1 victory over RB Leipzig, Bayer Leverkusen ending Freiburg’s unbeaten start and newly promoted Elversberg winning a seven-goal thriller against Augsburg, three key storylines. Eintracht Frankfurt also returned to winning ways against Cologne, while Mainz secured an important away victory at Schalke. Here are five players whose individual performances made the difference for their teams. Luis Díaz – Bayern Munich Luis Díaz delivered the standout performance of the weekend as Bayern Munich demolished RB Leipzig 6-1 at the Allianz Arena. The Colombian completed a hat-trick with goals in the 11th, 46th and 68th minutes, helping Vincent Kompany’s side respond emphatically after consecutive Bundesliga draws. Aleksandar Pavlović, Michael Olise and Harry Kane also scored, but Díaz was the main protagonist. His direct running, movement inside the penalty area and clinical finishing repeatedly exposed Leipzig’s defence. The victory also continued Bayern’s extraordinary goalscoring record at home, with 18 goals in their opening three Bundesliga matches at the Allianz Arena. Ibrahim Maza – Bayer Leverkusen Ibrahim Maza played a decisive role in Bayer Leverkusen’s 2-1 victory over Freiburg, ending Julian Schuster’s side’s unbeaten start to the season. After Derry Scherhant gave Freiburg an early lead, Maza equalised in the 19th minute. The Algerian international then produced the decisive attacking move in the second half, creating the opportunity for Patrik Schick to score the winner. While Schick deserves recognition for scoring in each of Leverkusen’s opening six Bundesliga matches, Maza’s goal and involvement in the winner made him the standout performer. His creativity and willingness to take responsibility in dangerous areas demonstrated why he is becoming increasingly important to Leverkusen’s attack. Here are five players whose individual performances made the difference for their teams. After Derry Scherhant gave Freiburg an early lead, Maza equalised in the 19th minute. The Algerian international then produced the decisive attacking move in the second half, creating the opportunity for Patrik Schick to score the winner. While Schick deserves recognition for scoring in each of Leverkusen’s opening six Bundesliga matches, Maza’s goal and involvement in the winner made him the standout performer. His creativity and willingness to take responsibility in dangerous areas demonstrated why he is becoming increasingly important to Leverkusen’s attack. Tietz – Mainz 05 Phillip Tietz proved decisive as Mainz secured an important away victory against Schalke on Matchday 6, extending their unbeaten record away from home in the Bundesliga this season. The striker scored the crucial goal that earned Mainz all three points, demonstrating his importance in a team that has struggled to find consistency during the opening weeks of the campaign. In the 24th minute, Tietz converted Anthony Caci’s assist to score the only goal in Mainz’s 1-0 victory. It was his fifth Bundesliga goal in six appearances, underlining his excellent start to the campaign, and his best-ever start to date. More importantly, the result gave Urs Fischer’s side three wins from three away matches this season, extending their unbeaten away run in the Bundesliga to eight games. While Mainz have struggled for consistency at home, their impressive away form has become one of the most interesting stories of the opening six matchdays. Tietz’s goalscoring ability has been central to that success, making him one of the standout performers of the weekend. Lukas Petkov – Elversberg Lukas Petkov was instrumental in Elversberg’s thrilling 4-3 victory over Augsburg, a result that continued the newly promoted club’s impressive introduction to Bundesliga football. The Bulgarian international opened the scoring in the fourth minute, reacting quickest after Finn Dahmen saved his penalty. Elversberg raced into a 3-0 lead, but Augsburg fought back through Fabian Rieder and Michael Gregoritsch. With the visitors threatening another goal, Petkov provided the assist for Frederik Schmahl’s 89th-minute strike, which ultimately proved decisive despite Mert Kömür scoring shortly afterwards. A goal and an assist in such an unpredictable encounter highlighted Petkov’s importance to Vincent Wagner’s attacking system. Miro Muheim – Hamburg For the second consecutive Bundesliga weekend, Miro Muheim emerged as Hamburg’s match-winner. The Swiss international scored a spectacular long-range goal in the 88th minute to secure a 1-0 victory over Stuttgart at the Volksparkstadion. Stuttgart had dominated much of the encounter and created numerous opportunities, but Hamburg remained organised defensively before Muheim produced the decisive moment with a powerful strike from approximately 25 metres. Having also scored the late winner against Hoffenheim on Matchday 5, Muheim has now delivered consecutive match-winning goals, helping Hamburg record three successive Bundesliga victories for the first time in 16 years. His performances have been particularly important for a team looking to establish itself after returning to Germany’s top flight. Matchday 6 offered a fascinating contrast between individual brilliance and decisive contributions under pressure. Díaz’s hat-trick dominated the headlines, Maza inspired Leverkusen, Petkov helped Elversberg survive a dramatic comeback, and Muheim once again delivered when Hamburg needed him most. These performances demonstrate how individual quality can shape matches, regardless of whether it comes from established international stars or players making their mark with less-fancied Bundesliga clubs. GGFN | Felipe

item.title: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama reveals what led to his ugly Opening Night vs. Thunder
item.description: Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama reveals what led to his ugly Opening Night vs. Thunder appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Victor Wembanyama just had one of the worst games of his professional career during the San Antonio Spurs ’ 116-104 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder on the opening night of the 2026-27 season. Wembanyama did have 12 points, 13 rebounds, and six blocks on the night, so it wasn’t all bad. But the Spurs star went just 1-of-13 from the field and missed all four of his three-point attempts on the night, living on the foul line to get his points. It wasn’t until the end of the third quarter that Wembanyama would score his only field goal — a dunk off a lob pass from De’Aaron Fox. All night long, the Spurs star was out of sorts, and the Thunder defense deserves credit for frustrating him to the point of being very passive, especially during the fourth quarter. At the end of the day, Wembanyama felt as though he was simply overthinking it and didn’t have much fun out there on the court as a result — leading to a rough night overall. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I need to go back to playing the basketball I like. This is not the sport I like, right here. I’ve got no reason to be hesitant. It’s as simple as that. I’m good when I have fun. I was indecisive. I might be overthinking it,” Wembanyama said in his postgame presser, via Oh No He Didn’t on X. Wemby on his offensive struggles tonight: "I need to go back to playing the basketball I like. This is not the sport I like, right here. I've got no reason to be hesitant. It's as simple as that. I'm good when I have fun. I was indecisive. I might be overthinking it" pic.twitter.com/dbuokBo8BV — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) October 21, 2026 Last season, Wembanyama was playing fast and loose, which must have been easier to do considering that the expectations for the Spurs weren’t nearly as high as they are heading into this upcoming campaign. Now, Wembanyama has to get used to dealing with the pressure of being the best player on a team with championship expectations. It does not help as well that the Spurs came so close to winning it all but fumbled multiple opportunities to defeat the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals. But considering how talented and driven Wembanyama is , expect him to return back to his usual ways in no time — making this opening night disaster a mere aberration. Related: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama calls out issues that got Thunder ‘having fun’ Related: Spurs’ Stephon Castle opens up on ‘hardest part’ of defending Sha Gilgeous-Alexander

item.title: Adam Silver answers if LeBron James’ helicopter rides have any ‘rule issues’
item.description: Credit: Jemal Countess for Fortune Media/Ishika Samant via Getty Images NBA Commissioner Adam Silver finally revealed if LeBron James is breaking any league rules. Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James’ decision to commute back and forth to games using a helicopter has sparked major debate in the NBA community. So much so that many fans want James’ helicopter deal with Fanatics to be investigated properly, as they believe the league will find evidence of wrongdoing. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver has finally put these rumours to bed by sharing his honest thoughts on James’ lucrative deal. Adam Silver says LeBron James’ helicopter deal is within NBA rules Ahead of the 76ers’ season-opener against the New York Knicks, Silver finally broke his silence on James’ viral helicopter deal. “I would just say in the case of LeBron and that helicopter, he has a deal with Fanatics,” Silver said. “It’s perfectly appropriate if part of his deal is that they’re gonna supply a helicopter to him as long as it’s just a deal between Fanatics and LeBron and no team is involved; there’s no rules issue there whatsoever.” Well, there you have it, as long as the 76ers aren’t involved in this deal, the NBA has no jurisdiction to investigate James. A big reason why fans are doubtful about James’ helicopter sponsorship is that Toronto Raptors star Kawhi Leonard and the LA Clippers were found guilty of a salary cap circumvention scandal. This led to a heavy punishment for both Leonard and the Clippers, but it doesn’t feel like a similar fate is waiting for James and the 76ers. Read more: Knicks fan’s ’go get Jesus’ jibe at LeBron James and 76ers backfires after 0-1 start ‘He has lost’: Skip Bayless says he just has one takeaway from LeBron James’ 76ers debut Nick Nurse says Mike Brown’s the only former LeBron James coach he didn’t call after signing

item.title: Alexis Mac Allister shines in Liverpool win over Villarreal
item.description: Alexis Mac Allister shines in Liverpool win over Villarreal Alexis Mac Allister scored twice to guide Liverpool to a thrilling 4-3 victory against Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday. Manager Andoni Iraola made six changes to the team that defeated Brentford 2-1 at the weekend. Iraola’s plan did not seem to work as Liverpool conceded twice inside the opening half-hour. George Mikautaze pounced on an error from Virgil van Dijk to open the scoring before Sergi Cardona added another with a fine finish. Mac Allister initiated Liverpool’s comeback by heading home Kostas Tsimikas’ corner. Ronald Araujo and Rio Ngumoha then combined to level the scores on the stroke of half-time. Mac Allister put Liverpool ahead after the hour mark, sweeping home a pinpoint cross from Ngumoha. Tani Oluwaseyi pulled one back to threaten a draw but the hosts held on to secure maximum points and join Paris Saint-Germain at the top of the Champions League table. Mac Allister admitted last month he felt ‘very sad’ that the Merseyside club declined to offer him a new contract. The Argentine confirmed he had offers to leave in the summer, but he opted to stay because of his love for Liverpool. Since making those comments, Mac Allister has been producing impressive displays on the pitch. If he continues his current form, there is no reason why Liverpool will not choose to extend his deal.

item.title: Hansi Flick’s decisions against PSG give Real Madrid major clues ahead of El Clasico
item.description: Hansi Flick’s decisions against PSG give Real Madrid major clues ahead of El Clasico Real Madrid’s upcoming El Clasico seems to have played an important role in Hansi Flick’s decisions during Barcelona’s 4-2 defeat to PSG. The German manager very clearly prioritised the fitness of several key players ahead of Sunday’s showdown. The Barcelona coach admitted after the match that the Clasico had influenced his team selection and rotations. Flick protects key players ahead of Real Madrid clash The clearest indication came before kick-off, when Rodri was surprisingly left out of Barcelona’s starting line-up. The midfielder did not feel ready to sustain maximum intensity for 90 minutes, prompting Flick to start Marc Bernal instead. Rodri eventually entered the match once the tempo had dropped, although he still appeared uncomfortable. Flick subsequently confirmed that the midfielder would feature against Madrid. Rodri was rested against PSG with a view of El Clasico. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Pedri and Raphinha were also withdrawn around the hour mark, limiting their workload ahead of the weekend. Raphinha’s substitution was particularly understandable given his limited involvement against Real Betis and his recent return from injury. Flick also replaced Xavi Espart in the 74th minute, seemingly unwilling to risk another defensive setback. Barca are clearly wary of Real Madrid Barcelona have one more day than Real Madrid to prepare for the Clasico, and yet they have shown how wary they are. Mourinho, on the other hand, is not planning any rotations tonight. Sunday’s fixture influenced Barcelona’s approach against PSG, and this gives Los Blancos much more incentive. Even facing the reigning European champions, Flick felt compelled to manage the minutes of several important players. That underlines the importance of the Clasico and the physical concerns surrounding Barcelona’s squad. Hansi Flick has shown how wary he is of Real Madrid ahead of El Clasico. (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images) However, Madrid will know better than to mistake Flick’s caution for weakness. Barca will come out all guns blazing against Los Blancos. By protecting Pedri, Raphinha and Rodri, the German may have improved his chances of fielding a stronger line-up on Sunday. The six-point gap makes this a particularly important opportunity for Madrid to regain ground in the title race. Should they fail to win on Sunday, they run the risk of dropping nine points behind the defending La Liga champions. Barca’s preparations have clearly been shaped by the Clasico. Now, the onus is on Madrid to ensure that the attention Flick has given to Sunday’s encounter does not pay off.

item.title: Flick talks Olmo, Espart, Joan Garcia, Rodri, Bernal, El Clasico after PSG 4-2 Barcelona
item.description: Flick talks Olmo, Espart, Joan Garcia, Rodri, Bernal, El Clasico after PSG 4-2 Barcelona Barcelona manager Hansi Flick has insisted that his team’s 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain can provide valuable lessons ahead of Sunday’s El Clasico, acknowledging that the European champions exposed areas his side must improve. The loss marked Barcelona’s first defeat of the 2026/27 season, with Luis Enrique’s PSG making the most of their attacking quality to overcome the Catalan side. Despite the disappointing result, Flick refused to overlook the positives, praising Xavi Espart and Joan Garcia while explaining his decision to rest Rodri ahead of the meeting with Real Madrid. Flick admits PSG exposed Barcelona’s weaknesses Barcelona struggled to contain PSG’s attack, especially as the game progressed, but Flick saw the contest as an important test of his team’s current level. “It was a great test for us and today we saw in which areas we need to improve. I also saw some good things,” he began. The German coach acknowledged that mistakes and turnovers had contributed to the defeat, while giving credit to PSG for their performance. “I think it was a fantastic game from both teams. We made mistakes and lost possession that we need to analyse,” Flick explained. He added that “PSG showed they were better than us. We lost, but we learned a lot from this match.” Hansi Flick praised Joan Garcia’s performance. (Photo by Catherine Steenkeste for Qatar Airways/Getty Images) With Real Madrid next on Barcelona’s schedule, Flick will have little time to address those shortcomings. He nevertheless stressed that the PSG encounter was important in its own right, rather than simply a warm-up for the weekend’s showdown. “Yes. Today’s match was important too. We didn’t want to lose. We had chances after the score was 1–1. PSG played fantastically. On Sunday it’s El Clasico, and that’s always important for us.” Xavi Espart and Joan Garcia earn Flick’s praise One of Barcelona’s brighter performers was Xavi Espart, who impressed at right-back against a formidable attacking opponent. Flick highlighted the youngster’s development and the level he has maintained since stepping up from youth football. “Xavi Espart is playing at an incredible level. I think I was surprised by his level last year, then the Under-19 European Championship and then he came directly to us. Since then he has played at a high level,” he noted. The manager also underlined the difficulty of Espart’s defensive assignment against PSG. “It wasn’t easy for Xavi Espart to defend today, and he played at an enormous level. We have to focus on the positives, and there were positives. Playing like that from right-back wasn’t easy,” he added. Goalkeeper Joan Garcia was another player to receive recognition after keeping Barcelona competitive with several important interventions. Flick explained the decision to start Marc Bernal ahead of Rodri. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) “PSG had many chances and Joan was fantastic,” Flick said. Flick also provided a brief update on Dani Olmo, who suffered a knock during the match , although the midfielder’s condition remains unclear. “Olmo took a knock and is feeling some pain. We’ll have to wait and see.” Rodri rested as Bernal makes his case before El Clasico Flick’s midfield selection also attracted attention, with Marc Bernal starting in place of Rodri. The decision was intended to manage the latter’s workload and ensure he would be fresher for the trip to face Real Madrid. “I spoke to him this morning to tell Rodri that Bernal would play. We are aware of Rodri’s fatigue and the minutes he has accumulated,” explained the manager. Lastly, Flick said that he was satisfied with Bernal’s contribution, particularly during the opening half, and reiterated the benefit of giving Rodri time to recover. “Bernal played and had a good game, especially in the first half, and Rodri will be fresh for the Clasico,” Flick concluded. Source: Mundo Deportivo

item.title: Chromiak’s game-winning goal leads Reign to first home win of the season
item.description: ONTARIO, CA. -- Martin Chromiak’s game-tying and game-winning goals led the Ontario Reign to a 3-2 victory against the Calgary Wranglers Tuesday night. Coming into tonight’s matchup, the eighth place Reign - who hadn’t won a home game yet - were undoubtedly the underdogs against first place Wranglers (5-3-0; 10 points). But tonight the crowd was able to see the win they deserved and a team whose mission was clear. “No one liked the game against Henderson ,” Chromiak said. “So we had a good practice, we got right back to it and I thought it was a much better effort from everyone. We played the whole 60 (minutes) and got the job done.” The Reign finally began the opening period in a way they had struggled to so far this season - with energy and aggression. Ontario had 12 shots on goal in the first period, which was much better than the four shots on goal in last game’s opening period. “You could tell right from the drop of the puck we were ready to go,” Ontario coach Andrew Lord said. “We’re playing faster, way more energy on the bench. It was a really good performance against a really, really good team.” Both teams were scoreless and hadn’t committed any penalties through the opening period, however that wouldn’t last much longer. Once again, the Reign allowed their opponent to score first on home ice. Tyson Gross found the back of the net with assists from William Stömgren and Axel Hurtig just two minutes into period two. It wasn’t until the Reign had the extra man advantage midway through the second period in which Cole Guttman tied the game with a power-play goal with help from Scott Perunovich and Chromiak. Rory Kerins was able to get the puck in the back of the net just seven seconds before intermission, giving the lead back to the Wranglers. Chromiak’s game-tying goal came 18 seconds into the final period and his game-winning goal at 17:10, giving the Reign a much needed home win. “I’m happy that the coaches trust me and they’re putting me out there,” Chromiak said. “Today was me, next game it could be someone else.” Ontario goalie Carter George earned his second win of the season with 24 saves. Lord describes the 20-year-old goalie as: “Electric. (He) reads the game so well, so poised, so calm. Such an old man demeanor for such a young kid and it’s really impressive. It’s fun to be a part of it.” This win brings Ontario up to third place in the AHL Pacific Division at 4-2-0 and 8 points. Ontario will visit the Texas Stars (1-3-1-1; 4 points) for a weekend series on Friday and Saturday, with each game beginning at 5 p.m. PT.

item.title: Celtic has that mentality to score in the last minute and Rangers don’t says Mulgrew
item.description: Celtic has that mentality to score in the last minute and Rangers don’t says Mulgrew Charlie Mulgrew is backing Celtic to have the edge in the title race, and the famous supercomputer agrees with winning Tennent’s Sixes skipper… Benjamin Nygren of Celtic celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026 (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Former Celtic star Charlie Mulgrew believes his old club have the edge over the Rangers when it comes to winning this season’s Scottish Premiership title race. Mulgrew suggests that in a direct head-to-head match up, the latest Ibrox club would be favourites to win, but Celtic’s experience and determination will see them collect more points over the course of the season. Speaking on the Go Radio Football Show , he said: “They’ve done it that many times last year under Martin O’Neill. “I just feel that they’ve got that mentality to score at the last minute, and I’m still questioning Rangers, whether they do.” Despite his belief in Celtic’s resilience, he acknowledged Rangers’ strength, saying: “It’s funny, when I think of Celtic playing Rangers tomorrow, I think Rangers are favourites in my mind. Martin O’Neill, Manager of Celtic, looks on before the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) “But when I think of Celtic playing any other team, and Rangers playing any other team, I always fancy Celtic to win.” His belief in Celtic’s ability to secure last-minute victories is unwavering. Charlie explained: “I think if you put it down to the last ten minutes of a game, Celtic and Rangers both drawing… I would fancy Celtic to go and get that last-minute winner. “I feel that they’ve got that.” “I feel like they’ve got that mentality to score in the last minute and Rangers don’t” In other news the much reported Supercomputer is also inclined to agree with Mulgrew, overwhelmingly believing that the hoops are strong favourites to win the title for the 15th time in 16 seasons, an incredible run of domination that Scottish football has never seen before. item.title: Liverpool closer to signing 'prime target' after major news emerges from Anfield
item.description: Liverpool closer to signing 'prime target' after major news emerges from Anfield Andoni Iraola's men have been linked with several new players this season. Although plenty of money was spent by Liverpool in the summer, more changes need to be made. Many different options have emerged for the Anfield outfit and, while some are genuinely exciting, others are a tad questionable. Obviously, because the Reds have spent so much money over the last couple of seasons, they're likely to be a tad hindered in terms of what they can and can't do. That's why, last summer, so many members of their first-team squad were moved on. And, although things have got better, there are always going to be ways for things to improve. Kees Smit's new contract means Liverpool aren't likely to sign him For some time now, Liverpool's fanbase have been demanding that their club brings in a new midfielder. Ever since Fabinho exited Anfield, things just haven't been the same. And, even though others such as Ryan Gravenberch and Alexis Mac Allister have been used to plug the gap left by the Brazilian, neither of them compare to what it would be like for Liverpool to have a natural number six. Several different players have emerged as potential options with AZ Alkmaar's Kees Smit being one of them . Throughout the summer, others were also linked but, now that the Dutchman has signed a new deal with the Eredivisie outfit until 2030, their move for him can be ruled out. Obviously, signing the 20-year-old would have been a huge risk as he's never played outside of his home country but, now that move is off the table, it feels like Liverpool may have been pushed closer to signing Alex Scott . Alex Scott is Liverpool's 'prime target' for midfield Of all the players linked with Liverpool, the transfer of Scott makes the most sense. The Englishman already knows how to play in Iraola's system and, since he's still only 23 years old, he has almost all of his career still ahead of him, which is why he's now the Reds' "prime target." This term, he managed to pick straight back up from where he left off last season and has quickly proven why he's one of Bournemouth's most important players. The fact that the former Bristol City man is also homegrown makes a huge difference as, it means that Liverpool would be able to sign him without getting rid of anyone. As, one of the other main problems that they're facing at the moment is the lack of homegrown talent that they have among their ranks. All of these reasons are just further proof why Scott is the one for Liverpool and, now that a deal for Smit is off the table, it's one less player for Liverpool to think about signing which means that they could be edging closer to signing Scott.

item.title: LeBron James' 76ers beat Knicks on NBA opening night
item.description: LeBron James is a four-time NBA champion and the league's all-time leading scorer [Getty Images] LeBron James scored 14 points on his debut for the Philadelphia 76ers as they defeated champions the New York Knicks on the NBA season's opening night. The 41-year-old James, entering a record-extending 24th season in the league with his fourth team after his summer move from the LA Lakers, also racked up seven assists as his new side triumphed 106-100. Tyrese Maxey top-scored with 28 points for the 76ers, while Jaylen Brown, who also made his debut after joining the 76ers from the Boston Celtics in a high profile trade for Paul George, scored 19 points with eight rebounds and six assists. The Knicks enjoyed title celebrations prior to the match, raising their third title banner to the rafters at Madison Square Garden in the presence of a crowd that included celebrity Knicks fans Ben Stiller and Spike Lee. The Knicks ended a 53-year title drought with their victory over the San Antonio Spurs in last season's NBA Finals but were unable to open their season with a win as the 76ers held out after taking the lead in the third quarter. Jalen Brunson led the scoring for the Knicks with 21 points and Karl-Anthony Towns picked up 19 points with 12 rebounds. "I could be a lot better," James told broadcaster NBC. "Still getting my rhythm, obviously just a little bit over two weeks with the new squad. "But I like the way we played. I think we played exceptionally well, especially defensively." In the opening match of the NBA's 81st season, the Detroit Pistons fought back in the second half to win 121-113 against the Boston Celtics. Cade Cunningham and Jalen Duren added 22 points each and Duncan Robinson scored 15 of his 21 in the fourth quarter as the home side secured their victory with a 23-0 scoring run. Celtics debutant Paul George scored 38 points for his new side in a match between last season's top two regular-season teams. In the night's final encounter, back-to-back NBA most valuable player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 32 points for the Oklahoma City Thunder as they completed a 116-104 win over the San Antonio Spurs. Stephon Castle top-scored for the Spurs with 24 points but his side were unable to match the form that saw them put out defending champions Thunder in last season's Western Conference finals. Victor Wembanyama made just one basket in 13 attempts for the Spurs but contributed 13 rebounds and six blocked shots and scored 12 points largely thanks to 10 free throws. "Obviously, this is the team that eliminated us from achieving our goal," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "But for us, I think it was more like we're just happy to be back. It's a longer summer when you don't win and we felt that this summer." The New York Knicks received their title rings from Walt 'Clyde' Frazier, a member of the franchise's previous title-winning teams in 1970 and 1973 [Getty Images]

item.title: The Newcastle United formation that Matthias Jaissle needs to cure these obvious flaws?
item.description: Newcastle United Team Huddle 2026 I believe the Newcastle United formation needs to be a 4-5-1, especially away from home. Also at home against the technically-better and possession-based sides. A 4-5-1 Newcastle United formation makes sense because they are rubbish at pressing and have a clear counter-attacking plan. They need to win the ball in midfield and then release quick wingers and mobile forwards. When attacking, they can shift into a 4-3-3 with the wingers pushing up. When defending, they can drop into a 4-5-1 block . They will just have to make sure that they don’t sit too deep and invite too much sustained pressure and they will have to rely on more players contributing goals. The recent results and performances show that they are in dire need of being compact and resilient. Two banks of four will make Newcastle United difficult to play through and outnumbering the opposition in the middle of the park can be useful against the common trend of Pep-based teams playing out from the back. A 4-5-1 would mean playing with two dominant holding midfielders (Gonzalez and Steur), or two athletic box-to-box players (two from three of Willock, Joelinton, Ramsey) two wingers (two from three of Harvey Barnes, Matias Fernandez-Pardo , Anthony Elanga), and a mobile forward (Osula or Wissa). All of these players need to be goal threats who can time their runs into the box. Now the problem is that the system depends heavily on a striker who can hold the ball up, win aerial duels, or create chances on their own. Will Osula is the only forward who could play this target man role and be able to occupy two centre backs. But he has his weaknesses. Is he really comfortable on the ball? Alternatively, you can play a false 9 with this system who drops off the front line into the midfield spaces and is closer to teammates for better link-up play. For example, Jacob Ramsey is quick-thinking, has the passing vision, close control, and the movement to unsettle defenders as a false 9. Even though you lose a target man and render crosses and long balls somewhat ineffective, when a centre-back follows the false 9 into midfield, a gap opens behind him for the midfielders and/or the wingers to attack. When the centre back doesn’t follow, the false 9 has time and space to turn and play and bring others into the game. With the players they have in the team and the squad, Newcastle United are a mid-table side. A 4-5-1 Newcastle United formation would suit this mid-table side better and make the most of the player’s strengths. Source

item.title: Bruins Postgame: A Near-Perfect Road Trip, What Went Wrong Late
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Boston Bruins could not keep their win streak alive on Tuesday, but they finished their four-game road trip with seven of a possible eight points. The Bruins (7-2-1) ended their road trip with a 3-2 overtime loss to the Dallas Stars (5-3-1) on Tuesday night at American Airlines Center. Matt Poitras and James Hagens scored for the Bruins, but Mikko Rantanen ’s three goals stopped the Bruins short of their perfect road trip, including the overtime winner at the 3:52 mark of the fourth period. Also Read: Bruins’ Win Streak Ends With Overtime Loss to Stars Jeremy Swayman made 22 of 25 saves and finished with 0.87 goals saved above expected, according to Natural Stat Trick . “That’s a hard game to play, and I am really proud of the boys,” Swayman said to reporters in Dallas postgame. “They maintained a good, solid 60 minutes, so give a ton of credit to them for locking it down, playing our system right, and giving full effort at the end of this road trip.” Unlike their last two games, the Bruins scored first and had a lead after 20 minutes. But once again, the young players stepped up. Matt Poitras ’ good friend Frederic Brunet set up his fourth goal of the season, and James Hagens found the back of the net for his third NHL goal. However, toward the end of the game, the Bruins’ goal scorers found themselves stapled to the bench. Poitras did not see the ice for the last 10:41 of the game, while Hagens sat for the last 9:02. Although no one directly asked Sturm about keeping them on the bench, he acknowledged the growing pains that come with a youth movement. “Again, they still need to learn. You could see it, when you play a team like Dallas today, a lot of veterans, and it’s a little bit more [of a] playoff atmosphere. You could tell they made a little bit more mistakes than some other games, but it’s healthy, though,” Sturm said about integrating the younger players into a veteran lineup. “It’s just going to help them moving forward.” The Bruins did not record a shot in the last 16:35 of the game, finishing the third period with four shots and overtime with zero. They also held the Stars to just two shots in the third period, but one of them found the back of the net. The power play also went 0-for-4 on Tuesday night. Entering the game, the Stars’ penalty kill ranked inside the top five, but the Bruins only got three shots on Jake Oettinger , and none came during their first two attempts. “That was probably a little bit of the difference tonight,” Sturm said of the power play. “We couldn’t really find our rhythm, and they were very aggressive. We had opportunities to shoot, but we just didn’t.” The penalty kill went 2-for-3, but the Stars’ lone power play goal was the overtime winner. Pavel Zacha took a slashing call 2:28 into overtime, and the call did not sit well with the Bruins’ head coach. “I have to see it again, but yes,” Sturm said when asked if he was surprised by the call. “My first thought was the same

Also Read: Bruins’ Win Streak Ends With Overtime Loss to Stars Jeremy Swayman made 22 of 25 saves and finished with 0.87 goals saved above expected, according to Natural Stat Trick . “That’s a hard game to play, and I am really proud of the boys,” Swayman said to reporters in Dallas postgame. “They maintained a good, solid 60 minutes, so give a ton of credit to them for locking it down, playing our system right, and giving full effort at the end of this road trip.” Unlike their last two games, the Bruins scored first and had a lead after 20 minutes. But once again, the young players stepped up. Matt Poitras ’ good friend Frederic Brunet set up his fourth goal of the season, and James Hagens found the back of the net for his third NHL goal. However, toward the end of the game, the Bruins’ goal scorers found themselves stapled to the bench. Poitras did not see the ice for the last 10:41 of the game, while Hagens sat for the last 9:02. Although no one directly asked Sturm about keeping them on the bench, he acknowledged the growing pains that come with a youth movement. “Again, they still need to learn. You could see it, when you play a team like Dallas today, a lot of veterans, and it’s a little bit more [of a] playoff atmosphere. You could tell they made a little bit more mistakes than some other games, but it’s healthy, though,” Sturm said about integrating the younger players into a veteran lineup. “It’s just going to help them moving forward.” The Bruins did not record a shot in the last 16:35 of the game, finishing the third period with four shots and overtime with zero. They also held the Stars to just two shots in the third period, but one of them found the back of the net. The power play also went 0-for-4 on Tuesday night. Entering the game, the Stars’ penalty kill ranked inside the top five, but the Bruins only got three shots on Jake Oettinger , and none came during their first two attempts. “That was probably a little bit of the difference tonight,” Sturm said of the power play. “We couldn’t really find our rhythm, and they were very aggressive. We had opportunities to shoot, but we just didn’t.” The penalty kill went 2-for-3, but the Stars’ lone power play goal was the overtime winner. Pavel Zacha took a slashing call 2:28 into overtime, and the call did not sit well with the Bruins’ head coach. “I have to see it again, but yes,” Sturm said when asked if he was surprised by the call. “My first thought was the same thing; it’s overtime, and he still got a shot off. So I just got to see it again.” Nikita Zadorov , who played in his first game since being scratched for disciplinary reasons, chose his words a little more carefully. He said, “I think I’m going to stay away from talking about penalties,” to reporters postgame. Mikko Rantanen ’s overtime winner snapped the Bruins’ five-game win streak, but it did little to diminish what they accomplished over their four-game trip out west. “I don’t think we’ve ever swept the California road trip since I’ve been here. It’s a hard feat, and it’s hard to win in this league,” Swayman said. “This was a trip that, again, we were all laughing, like it’s been the best trip ever because of the camaraderie and the way we have competed and been able to stick together every single day.” The Bruins won all three games in California, including back-to-back games with four unanswered goals against the Ducks and Kings. They also got contributions throughout the lineup, with younger players taking on a bigger role and leaving their mark on the scoresheet throughout the trip. Even in Tuesday’s loss, the Bruins managed to limit a high-powered Dallas offense for much of the night. Zadorov praised the team’s defensive effort, even though they could not close out the road trip with a fourth win. “Obviously, we would like to get two points in that game. They are a really dangerous offensive team. You can see the skill, especially in their top-six and top-two defensemen,” Zadorov said. “I thought we did a pretty good job overall defensively to keep them away from the scoresheet, but on the power play in overtime, Mikko [Rantanen] made an unbelievable play there, so you just have to tip the hat there. But overall, a great trip for our team. We got seven out of eight points. So, it’s something to build off of, and now we have two big ones at home, so we are shifting focus to that.” The Bruins fly home on Wednesday ahead of a quick two-game homestand against the Nashville Predators and San Jose Sharks . Through 10 games, they still occupy the top spot in the Atlantic Division and now sit one point ahead of the Tampa Bay Lightning . item.title: ‘He’s Making Money Down The Future’ — Patriots Legend Rob Gronkowski Sees Big Things Coming For Buccaneers Rookie Jalon Daniels
item.description: ‘He’s Making Money Down The Future’ — Patriots Legend Rob Gronkowski Sees Big Things Coming For Buccaneers Rookie Jalon Daniels Quarterback Jalon Daniels began the 2026 season as an undrafted rookie, with little expectation that he would play a big role in the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ offense so early in his professional career. However, Baker Mayfield’s injury created an opportunity for Daniels to step into the spotlight. Daniels faced a tough challenge in Week 6 when the Buccaneers went up against the Pittsburgh Steelers, ultimately suffering a 26-19 loss in overtime, but New England Patriots legend Rob Gronkowski remains confident in the rookie’s potential. Rob Gronkowski Sees Long-Term Potential in Jalon Daniels Daniels had a rough outing against the Steelers, throwing two interceptions in the fourth quarter of the Buccaneers’ overtime loss. His performance took a big hit on the final play, as an unaccounted-for Jalen Ramsey broke through on a blitz to sack him on fourth down. He finished the game with 22 completions on 43 attempts for 164 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. He now ranks No. 30 in the league with a 64.6 PFN QB Impact Grade . The Steelers held a clear advantage in total offense, outgaining Tampa Bay 300-224, and Daniels didn’t look good in the game. However, Gronkowski had high praise for the rookie QB’s potential on “The Gronk & Jules Show” on Tuesday. “I really do like this guy Jalon Daniels,” Gronkowski said . “He definitely is playing himself into a backup role, if not a starting role in the future, or a backup role where it’s possible that you might be the starter this year. This is down the road. We’re talking three, four, five years. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “But this guy looks like he can be a journeyman at minimum for a long time. He’s definitely making money as the backup quarterback right now, starting for the Buccaneers. He’s making money down the future. And he’s very poised for an undrafted rookie, free agent quarterback and just how he handles himself and represents himself.” Across four appearances, he has thrown for 501 yards, three touchdowns, and five interceptions while also taking nine sacks. However, Daniels has proved that he can contribute to winning football, as he helped the Buccaneers secure their first win of the season in a primetime matchup against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5. He completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown, avoiding any interceptions as Tampa Bay came away with the win. item.title: Where to watch Hornets vs. Nets today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for NBA season opener
item.description: Where to watch Hornets vs. Nets today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for NBA season opener originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Hornets will travel to Brooklyn to take on the Nets for both teams' regular season kickoff on Wednesday night. After a preseason loss to the Nets on Oct. 6, Charlotte will be looking for an opposite result this week. The Hornets' recent struggles have been exacerbated by the loss of franchise star LaMelo Ball, and absence of guard Kon Knueppel, who is sidelined with a hamstring strain. This team shouldn't be counted out though — at full strength, they'll be strong. The Nets might have a bit of an upper hand here, especially given the home-court advantage. Michael Porter Jr. & Co. routed the Hornets in their preseason opener, 124-90, setting Brooklyn up for a 3-1 start. Can the Nets defend Barclays Center? You won't want to miss this. Here's everything you need to know about Hornets vs. Nets today, including TV channel and streaming options for the NBA season opener. Where to watch Hornets vs. Nets today TV channels: WSOC Channel 9 (Charlotte), Yes Network (Brooklyn) Live streams: DAZN (Hornets), DAZN (Nets) The Hornets-Nets game will be televised locally by Yes Network in Brooklyn, and WSOC Channel 9 in Charlotte. Those in the Charlotte market can also watch live and on-demand with DAZN . DAZN is Charlotte's new direct-to-consumer media partner, set to air preseason and regular-season games along with additional Hornets content all season long ( read more here ). All games not selected for exclusive national broadcast by one of the league's partners will be available to stream live and on-demand with DAZN, which offers a free trial for new subscribers. What time is Hornets vs. Nets today? Date: Wednesday, Oct. 21 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET The Nets and Hornets season opener is set to tip off Wednesday at 7:30 p.m. ET. The game will be played at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, NY. Hornets schedule 2026-27 Here are Charlotte's upcoming games: Date Game Time (ET) Oct. 21 at Nets 7:30 p.m. Oct. 23 vs. Hawks 7 p.m. Oct. 24 vs. Heat 6 p.m. Oct. 26 vs. Wizards 7 p.m. Oct. 28 at Pistons 7 p.m. Nets schedule 2026-27 Here are Brooklyn's upcoming games: Date Game Time (ET) Oct. 21 vs. Hornets 7:30 p.m. Oct. 24 at Cavaliers 7:30 p.m. Oct. 25 vs. Pacers 6 p.m. Oct. 27 at Celtics 7:30 p.m. Oct. 30 vs. Pistons 7:30 p.m. Related Links Latest NBA news and rumors Full NBA schedule, scores How to bet on the NBA The GOAT Debate: Michael Jordan vs. LeBron James

item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 19: James Maddison of Tottenham Hotspur celebrates scoring the first goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Coventry City at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 19, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Marc Atkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning everyone – Yes I know the Champions League happened, and continues to happen. So too does the EFL Championship and League One. But there’s nothing more important than the AP Top 25 preseason rankings for the NCAA Men’s College Basketball. Here’s the top 25: 1. Florida (47) 2. Duke (10) 3. Illinois (2) 4. UConn 5. Arizona 6. Michigan State 7. Texas 8. Tennessee 9. Virginia 10. Houston 11. Louisville 12. Arkansas 13. St. John’s 14. Miami (FL) 15. Gonzaga 16. Michigan 17. Kansas 18. Iowa State 19. Texas Tech 20. item.title: How England hopeful Acheampong is giving Chelsea a big decision to make
item.description: Acheampong has made 52 appearances since his debut for Chelsea in 2024 [Getty Images] Chelsea's academy has been a production line for England defenders, and Josh Acheampong could become the latest to take that step. Since John Terry broke through in the early 2000s, Chelsea have produced Levi Colwill, Trevoh Chalobah, Marc Guehi and Fikayo Tomori for England, while also developing international centre-backs Andreas Christensen and Nathan Ake. Acheampong has started six of Chelsea's past nine matches in all competitions. Only four players - attackers Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, and defenders Colwill and Maxence Lacroix - have played more than his 581 minutes under new manager Xabi Alonso. Much of that has stemmed from Alonso settling on a more consistent side. Chelsea had conceded a league-high 12 goals before the international break but have let in only one since, including recording their first clean sheet of the season away at Everton on Saturday. Acheampong, 20, has operated as a roaming centre-back in a back three alongside more fixed options Colwill and Lacroix, stepping into midfield or moving wide to perform the role of a traditional full-back when in possession. He has also developed a promising understanding with right wing-back Pedro Neto, combining with him in the move that led to Joao Pedro's goal against Bournemouth, while keeping £75m signing Wesley Fofana out of the side. Alonso has been keen to emphasise Chelsea's defensive improvement as a collective effort, with the return of Moises Caicedo from injury and his partnership alongside 36-year-old Jordan Henderson adding greater stability. During a pre-season tour of Australia and Asia, Alonso also hammered home his policy of giving minutes to those who most deserve it, rather than on reputation. It's in this environment Acheampong has begun featuring regularly, while also starting eight of England Under-21s' past 10 matches. Increasingly, the young defender appears to be knocking on the door of a senior call-up should manager Thomas Tuchel seek a versatile option on the right side of defence. Could Acheampong still leave Chelsea? Acheampong is under contract until 2029, meaning decisions need to be made between now and next summer. Across recent transfer windows, the defender has been repeatedly linked with moves away from Stamford Bridge, only for sources within Chelsea to insist he was "untouchable". That message has remained consistent, although it has occasionally raised eyebrows. item.content:encoded: Acheampong has made 52 appearances since his debut for Chelsea in 2024 [Getty Images] Chelsea's academy has been a production line for England defenders, and Josh Acheampong could become the latest to take that step. Since John Terry broke through in the early 2000s, Chelsea have produced Levi Colwill, Trevoh Chalobah, Marc Guehi and Fikayo Tomori for England, while also developing international centre-backs Andreas Christensen and Nathan Ake. Acheampong has started six of Chelsea's past nine matches in all competitions. Only four players - attackers Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, and defenders Colwill and Maxence Lacroix - have played more than his 581 minutes under new manager Xabi Alonso. Much of that has stemmed from Alonso settling on a more consistent side. Chelsea had conceded a league-high 12 goals before the international break but have let in only one since, including recording their first clean sheet of the season away at Everton on Saturday. Acheampong, 20, has operated as a roaming centre-back in a back three alongside more fixed options Colwill and Lacroix, stepping into midfield or moving wide to perform the role of a traditional full-back when in possession. He has also developed a promising understanding with right wing-back Pedro Neto, combining with him in the move that led to Joao Pedro's goal against Bournemouth, while keeping £75m signing Wesley Fofana out of the side. Alonso has been keen to emphasise Chelsea's defensive improvement as a collective effort, with the return of Moises Caicedo from injury and his partnership alongside 36-year-old Jordan Henderson adding greater stability. During a pre-season tour of Australia and Asia, Alonso also hammered home his policy of giving minutes to those who most deserve it, rather than on reputation. It's in this environment Acheampong has begun featuring regularly, while also starting eight of England Under-21s' past 10 matches. Increasingly, the young defender appears to be knocking on the door of a senior call-up should manager Thomas Tuchel seek a versatile option on the right side of defence. Could Acheampong still leave Chelsea? Acheampong is under contract until 2029, meaning decisions need to be made between now and next summer. Across recent transfer windows, the defender has been repeatedly linked with moves away from Stamford Bridge, only for sources within Chelsea to insist he was "untouchable". That message has remained consistent, although it has occasionally raised eyebrows. Chelsea seriously explored moves for now-Real Madrid defender Dean Huijsen in the summer of 2025 and Liverpool centre-back Jeremy Jacquet in January 2026, who possess similar attributes and are only a year older than Acheampong. At one stage during the summer Chelsea had 10 senior centre-backs on their books, before ending the transfer window with six. In a season without European football, there were genuine doubts over how much Acheampong would play. Potential loan moves were explored, including a switch to Crystal Palace. Palace instead signed Chelsea's Axel Disasi on loan, with Premier League rules permitting only one domestic loan signing from another top-flight club. Despite being with Chelsea since Under-8s, Acheampong has come close to leaving on more than one occasion. In 2023, he did not sign a professional contract on his 17th birthday, which is typically the norm for elite academy prospects. The club's current ownership later moved to secure his future in January 2024, avoiding the risk of losing him for only a nominal compensation fee. Twelve months later, Acheampong again appeared to be heading towards the exit in what former manager Enzo Maresca described as a "bad situation". Before the conclusion of lengthy and ultimately successful negotiations, the club's hierarchy withdrew him from selection at both academy and first-team level before he eventually signed a contract until 2029. That agreement, signed in December 2024, remains the deal he is on today. Chelsea could face important decisions next summer, when Acheampong, Colwill and Fofana will all enter the final two years of their contracts. Chalobah and Tosin Adarabioyo were sold to Como and Tottenham Hotspur respectively this summer after entering the final two years of their deals. The policy stems in part from lessons learned following Chelsea's 2022 takeover, when Antonio Rudiger and Christensen departed on free transfers to Real Madrid and Barcelona respectively. Those exits triggered a scramble to reinforce the centre of defence, contributing to expensive moves for Fofana and Marc Cucurella. Acheampong's recent performances have begun to attract wider recognition among Chelsea supporters and have raised the stakes surrounding his future. At present, there are no active discussions over a new deal, although the idea of a seven-year contract has been floated previously. There is caution within Acheampong's camp about rushing into negotiations until there is clearer evidence that he can become a regular starter at Chelsea. However, the first-team football provided by Alonso has given the club its strongest chance yet of persuading one of its most promising academy graduates to commit his long-term future. item.title: PSG fear that Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has ruptured his ACL
item.description: PSG fear that Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has ruptured his ACL There are growing fears within PSG that left-winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has ruptured the ACL in his right knee during Les Parisiens ‘ 4-2 home win in Matchday 3 of the UEFA Champions League against FC Barcelona (4-2) . L’Equipe reports that PGS are sweating over the fitness of the Georgian maverick, who played an instrumental role in leading PSG to two Champions League triumphs. Before the hour mark, Kvaratskhelia collided with Barcelona right-back Xavi Espart and immediately clutched his knee in serious pain. The 25-year-old Kvaratskhelia could not put any weight on his right foot and had to be carried off the pitch. The winger will undergo an MRI on Wednesday to know the extent of his injury. But PSG are fearing the worst. L’Equipe adds that members of Kvaratskhelia’s entourage feared an ACL tear following initial tests. Should the early diagnosis prove true, Kvaratskhelia could be set for a 6-month spell on the sidelines. GFFN | Bastien Cheval

item.title: Raiders vs Rams to feature two of NFL's top 5 passers
item.description: A few quarterbacks in the NFL came roaring out the gates to lead the league in passing yards early. Kirk Cousins didn't, but the 38-year-old may be proving the old addage that slow and steady wins the race. Sunday against the Bills , Cousins threw for over 300 yards for the second time in three weeks. And his consistent production thus far has now moved him inside the top five passing yards through six weeks of the season. While we give Cousins kudos for moving into the fifth spot, you may notice the name atop that list is the man who will be lining up behind center for the Raiders ' opponent next Sunday -- Matt Stafford. Where Cousins has Stafford beat, however, is touchdown passes. In fact, no one has more TD passes this season than the 14 by Kirko Chains. Brock Purdy and Trevor Lawrence each also have 14. Stafford has a respectable 11, which is tied for 11th in the league. We shall see this Sunday when the two of them take the same field if Cousins can move up the passing yards ranking or if Stafford can move up the TD pass rankings. This article originally appeared on Raiders Wire: Raiders vs Rams to feature two of NFL's top 5 passers
item.content:encoded: A few quarterbacks in the NFL came roaring out the gates to lead the league in passing yards early. Kirk Cousins didn't, but the 38-year-old may be proving the old addage that slow and steady wins the race. Sunday against the Bills , Cousins threw for over 300 yards for the second time in three weeks. And his consistent production thus far has now moved him inside the top five passing yards through six weeks of the season. While we give Cousins kudos for moving into the fifth spot, you may notice the name atop that list is the man who will be lining up behind center for the Raiders ' opponent next Sunday -- Matt Stafford. Where Cousins has Stafford beat, however, is touchdown passes. In fact, no one has more TD passes this season than the 14 by Kirko Chains. Brock Purdy and Trevor Lawrence each also have 14. Stafford has a respectable 11, which is tied for 11th in the league. We shall see this Sunday when the two of them take the same field if Cousins can move up the passing yards ranking or if Stafford can move up the TD pass rankings. This article originally appeared on Raiders Wire: Raiders vs Rams to feature two of NFL's top 5 passers

item.title: Dale Steyn’s 18-year-old record falls as Simon Harmer scripts history against Australia
item.description: Simon Harmer etched his name in South African cricket history with a career-best effort against Australia, breaking Dale Steyn’s record for the highest individual score by a South African No. 9 or lower against the visitors. Harmer scored 82 in South Africa’s first innings on Day 3 of the second Test at St George’s Park in Gqeberha on Tuesday, surpassing Steyn’s previous record of 76, made in Melbourne in 2008. The off-spinner struck 10 fours and a six in his 91-ball innings, providing crucial support to skipper Temba Bavuma as South Africa recovered from 110-6 to declare at 425-9. Harmer’s maiden Test half-century came at a pivotal stage after Australia had put the hosts under pressure. Bavuma and Marco Jansen had already combined for a 132-run stand for the seventh wicket before Jansen fell for 85. Harmer then joined Bavuma to add 183 runs for the eighth wicket, putting South Africa firmly back in control. It was the second-highest partnership for the eighth wicket or lower in South African Test history, behind Mark Boucher and Pat Symcox’s 195-run stand against Pakistan in Johannesburg in 1998. The partnership also moved past the 180-run stand between JP Duminy and Steyn against Australia in Melbourne in 2008, underlining the significance of Harmer’s contribution. Bavuma made 179, his highest Test score, after facing 334 deliveries and hitting 18 fours and a six. He had walked in with South Africa at 12-2 on the opening day and held the innings together through multiple batting collapses. Harmer’s innings ended when he was bowled by Marnus Labuschagne, leaving him short of a maiden Test century. South Africa declared soon after Bavuma was dismissed by Mitchell Starc. Australia were 3-1 at stumps after Kagiso Rabada dismissed Nic Maddinson for a four-ball duck late in the day. Australia won the first Test in Durban by 214 runs and lead the three-match series 1-0.
