item.title: Manchester City handed a huge boost ahead of Aston Villa clash with Erling Haaland available to play
item.description: Manchester City handed a huge boost ahead of Aston Villa clash with Erling Haaland available to play Manchester City cruised to a 5-1 victory over AEK Athens last night at the Etihad Stadium. A hat trick from Phil Foden and goals from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki sealed a comfortable win for Enzo Maresca’s side in their matchday three Champions League league phase fixture at the Etihad Stadium. City’s win was the ideal preparation for Manchester City’s upcoming Premier League fixture against Aston Villa at Villa Park on Saturday. Heading into this Saturday’s clash with Unai Emery’s side Manchester City have received a boost with Erling Haaland ready to play at Villa Park. Enzo Maresca has confirmed that Erling Haaland will be ready to play against Aston Villa. Erling Haaland was an unused substitute as Manchester City beat AEK Athens last night. The question heading into last night’s match was whether or not any of Erling Haaland, Nico O’Reilly, Matheus Nunes or Mateo Kovacic would be in City’s matchday squad for the match at the Etihad Stadium. Of the injured quartet, only Erling Haaland made the bench for the game. Speaking after his team swept AEK Athens aside, Enzo Maresca revealed that Erling Haaland is fit to start against Aston Villa. Speaking on Haaland’s availability for the match at Villa Park, Maresca said, in quotes relayed by The Manchester Evening News : “ He’s okay to start (Erling Haaland) on Saturday. We had five or six players on the bench who ready to go inside but at the same time they had a rest so we’re happy with that. ” Enzo Maresca’s side will need Erling Haaland as they face a tough test at Villa Park. Manchester City had almost the perfect night against AEK Athens at the Etihad Stadium last night. They cruised to a 5-1 win and several key players had the opportunity to rest. Erling Haaland had a much-needed rest. As did Jeremy Doku, Iliman Ndiaye, Marc Guehi and Ayyoub Bouaddi. The opportunity to rest key players is fleeting for Enzo Maresca. Thankfully that opportunity came along as it was taken. Up next for Manchester City is a tough trip to Villa Park to take on Aston Villa. Typically, City struggle against Unai Emery’s side at Villa Park. They haven’t won at the venue since a 2-1 win there back in December of 2021. Since then, City have lost three and drawn one at Villa Park. If Enzo Maresca’s side are to pick up all three points on Saturday and break their Villa Park hoodoo, they’ll need their key players to be fit, rested, and available. Enzo Maresca’s update on Erling Haaland’s fitness suggests that he will be ready to start on Saturday. Enzo Maresca has confirmed that Erling Haaland will be ready to start against Aston Villa at Villa Park on Saturday. It seems that Haaland’s injury issue is behind him. Also, he will be well rested for what looms as a tough test for Enzo Maresca’s side. That is another bonus of City’s comfortable win last night.

item.title: Darcy Kuemper gets real on Kings’ 1st win of the season
item.description: Candice Ward-Imagn Images Darcy Kuemper gets real on Kings’ 1st win of the season appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Kings lost Quinton Byfield to injury on Tuesday night against the Washington Capitals. At the time, the game was tied 2-2, and Los Angeles had a ton of pressure on them to see this one out. Darcy Kuemper and his teammates were able to do just that. The Kings rode a three-goal third period to victory on Tuesday night. Star winger Adrian Kempe scored twice for Los Angeles in this contest. Kuemper was solid in goal, making 30 saves on the night. After the game, the veteran goaltender opened up about finally having that first win of the year. “I don’t think it’s unusual for teams to go on losing streaks throughout the year, but when it’s at the start of the year, it gets magnified, and it feels a lot worse for us,” the Los Angeles goalie said, via NHL.com. “It looks a lot worse. So, nice to get a win, and now we just got to get rolling.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Kuemper has not had the best start to the season personally. He has an unsightly .869 save percentage after Tuesday’s win over the Capitals. However, it’s hard to argue with the performance. He was a rock in goal for Los Angeles, and he won the game when his team needed him. As the veteran netminder said, Los Angeles has to build on this performance. Stringing a few wins together certainly flips the narrative and gives Kings fans a new sign of hope for this season. They have a chance to make it two in a row when they take on the New York Islanders on October 22. Related: Kings lose Quinton Byfield to injury vs. Capitals

item.title: Thunder star SGA gets 100% real on simple approach that helped OKC rip Spurs apart
item.description: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images Thunder star SGA gets 100% real on simple approach that helped OKC rip Spurs apart appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Shai Gilgeous-Alexander picked up right where he left off against the San Antonio Spurs , and he made his approach sound about as simple as it gets. The Oklahoma City Thunder superstar poured in 32 points on 13-of-27 shooting, adding five rebounds and four assists, as the Thunder beat the Spurs 116-104 on Tuesday night at Frost Bank Center . Speaking with NBC after the game, The two-time NBA MVP was asked how he found his rhythm so quickly in the season opener. “This is the game I love. I work hard in the summertime. I come out here and trust my work. It’s that simple. It’s not more complicated than that,” Gilgeous-Alexander said. “I come out here with the utmost confidence because of how hard I work, and I trust it every night, and it’s been working for me lately.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "I come out here and trust my work; it's that simple." Shai Gilgeous-Alexander after the Thunder's opening-night win over the Spurs 🗣️ (via @NBAonNBC ) pic.twitter.com/f5lbs9y4kS — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 21, 2026 The win carried extra meaning. The opener was a rematch of last season’s Western Conference Finals, when the Spurs eliminated Oklahoma City with a 111-103 win in Game 7. “Obviously this is the team that eliminated us from achieving our goal, but for us I think it was more we’re just happy to be back,” Gilgeous-Alexander said. “It’s a longer summer when you don’t win, and we felt that this summer.” Gilgeous-Alexander was quick to keep the result in perspective. “One of 82, like, this doesn’t prove anything,” he said. “We took a step in the right direction, and we got to do it 81 more times and be ready for the playoffs.” The Thunder controlled the game for most of the night. Oklahoma City built a 21-point halftime lead, and after the Spurs cut it to single digits in the third quarter, Gilgeous-Alexander helped push it back to double digits in the fourth. Victor Wembanyama was held to 12 points on 1-of-13 shooting . Gilgeous-Alexander also made it clear that the sting of last season’s exit is still being felt. “This group’s hungry. This group wants more. This group’s not satisfied, a little bit more so than in the past,” he said. “I can feel it. We feel it in the building. We feel it in the facility.” Oklahoma City will look to keep that hunger going when it faces the Denver Nuggets on Thursday. Related: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama calls out issues that got Thunder ‘having fun’ Related: Thunder HC Mark Daigneault speaks up on defense that Victor Wembanyama couldn’t solve

The opener was a rematch of last season’s Western Conference Finals, when the Spurs eliminated Oklahoma City with a 111-103 win in Game 7. “Obviously this is the team that eliminated us from achieving our goal, but for us I think it was more we’re just happy to be back,” Gilgeous-Alexander said. “It’s a longer summer when you don’t win, and we felt that this summer.” Gilgeous-Alexander was quick to keep the result in perspective. “One of 82, like, this doesn’t prove anything,” he said. “We took a step in the right direction, and we got to do it 81 more times and be ready for the playoffs.” The Thunder controlled the game for most of the night. Oklahoma City built a 21-point halftime lead, and after the Spurs cut it to single digits in the third quarter, Gilgeous-Alexander helped push it back to double digits in the fourth. Victor Wembanyama was held to 12 points on 1-of-13 shooting . Gilgeous-Alexander also made it clear that the sting of last season’s exit is still being felt. “This group’s hungry. This group wants more. This group’s not satisfied, a little bit more so than in the past,” he said. “I can feel it. We feel it in the building. We feel it in the facility.” Oklahoma City will look to keep that hunger going when it faces the Denver Nuggets on Thursday. item.title: Spurs’ Stephon Castle opens up on ‘hardest part’ of defending Sha Gilgeous-Alexander
item.description: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images Spurs’ Stephon Castle opens up on ‘hardest part’ of defending Sha Gilgeous-Alexander appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Oklahoma City Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander demonstrated in the NBA season opener why he has been crowned the league’s MVP in back-to-back seasons. SGA dominated Stephon Castle and the San Antonio Spurs , leading the Thunder to a 116-104 win to begin the season. Castle was also candid about the difficulty of defending the Oklahoma City superstar . Following the disappointing Opening Night loss , Castle opened up about the challenge of guarding SGA, explaining how difficult it was to contain the reigning MVP without committing unnecessary fouls. “Really trying to be physical with him, but physical enough that you don’t bait yourself into a foul,” Castle said. “That’s probably the hardest part. But it’s not really an individual thing; it’s more of a team thing.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) With Gilgeous-Alexander leading the charge, Oklahoma City asserted its dominance in the first half and headed into the break with a 65-44 advantage. Castle and De’Aaron Fox tried to shoulder the offensive responsibility as the Spurs looked to mount a comeback, but the defending champions maintained their rhythm and held on to secure a 12-point victory. Castle paced San Antonio with 24 points, shooting 9-of-21 from the field and 5-of-12 from beyond the arc, while also grabbing seven rebounds in 28 minutes. However, one of the biggest disappointments for Spurs fans on Tuesday was Victor Wembanyama’s underwhelming performance, particularly his struggles to find his shooting touch against the Thunder. On the other side, SGA’s scoring prowess helped Oklahoma City maintain control and withstand San Antonio’s second-half rally. He wrapped up the game with 32 points, six rebounds, four assists, three steals and three blocks. The Spurs entered the new season after a season in which they demonstrated their strength during the regular season before reaching the NBA Finals for the first time in a decade. Though San Antonio ultimately fell short of winning the championship, fans still expected the young team to make a strong start to the new campaign. Now, it remains to be seen whether this disappointing opening-night loss will motivate the Spurs to respond with greater determination in their upcoming games. Related: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama calls out issues that got Thunder ‘having fun’ Related: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama reveals what led to his ugly Opening Night vs. Thunder

item.title: Mail: Man Utd to kickstart 2027 rebuild by activating player’s 12-month option before selling him
item.description: Mail: Man Utd to kickstart 2027 rebuild by activating player’s 12-month option before selling him Manchester United have made plans to part ways with Lisandro Martinez in the summer of 2027. MailSport claims that United’s defensive rebuild at the end of the season will ‘signal the end’ of the centre-half’s Old Trafford career. Lisandro Martinez: The state of play (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) If that does indeed prove to be the case, it will see the Argentine’s tenure come to an end after five years. During that time, he will not have overseen a single campaign injury-free. With Martinez ruled out of tonight’s clash with Como , it’ll take his tally up to a whopping 90 games missed across all competitions for the club, which has also seen him limited to just 118 appearances in that time. Lisandro Martinez has started 41 of possible 115 PL games for #mufc since September 2023 (36%) [sky] pic.twitter.com/8YV3INeJWA When at his best, there is no disputing that the 28-year-old is a formidable figure to have at the back, but he is simply far too unreliable for a manager to depend upon throughout the course of a term. Why are United wanting to sell Martinez? (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Yet, it’s naive to think his torrid injury record is the main reason INEOS want to offload Martinez. His outburst in Madrid last week, during which he directly called out the board and Director of Football Jason Wilcox for their lack of investment, will have swayed their decision-making when mulling over his future. It’s thought that they will activate the 12-month option in his contract, as it’s currently due to expire in June 2027, before transfer-listing him and seeing what bids arrive. Breaking: Lisandro Martinez on Instagram: pic.twitter.com/AekB687KMS That way, United will ensure they get at least some fee for a player they shelled out £48.3 million for. Reports have suggested that Martinez was eyeing a move to Atletico Madrid before 2026/2027 got underway so that he could follow his close friend and compatriot Cristian Romero to the Spanish giants, and they would still be his first choice when the window reopens. item.title: Rival watch: Barcelona suffer major injury blow ahead of El Clasico vs Real Madrid
item.description: Rival watch: Barcelona suffer major injury blow ahead of El Clasico vs Real Madrid Real Madrid are preparing to face Barcelona at the Spotify Camp Nou in the first El Clasico of the season later this week. Hansi Flick’s men have a perfect record in the league so far and a six-point advantage over their arch-rivals ahead of the game. However, they are coming into the Clasico on the back of a 4-2 loss to PSG in the Champions League, which may have disrupted their momentum. Los Blancos ’ upcoming El Clasico against Barça could take place without Dani Olmo after the Spain international picked up an injury at the Parc des Princes. According to Diario AS , initial assessments suggest the 28-year-old Barça superstar has suffered a possible left adductor tear. The midfielder is expected to undergo an MRI scan on Wednesday to confirm the diagnosis. Olmo’s injury adds to Barcelona’s problems Olmo started against PSG ahead of Fermin Lopez, marking his 100th appearance for Barcelona, but had to be withdrawn after a challenge from Vitinha. He immediately indicated that he could not continue and was replaced by Fermin Lopez in the 27th minute. Dani Olmo is unlikely to be available for Barcelona against Real Madrid. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Although Barcelona have not confirmed the extent of the injury, his participation in Sunday’s Clasico appears highly unlikely. The midfielder previously suffered an adductor problem during the 2024-25 season, which kept him out for approximately three weeks. His injury adds to an already growing injury list for Barça , with Andreas Christensen, Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde also currently unfit. The Frenchman is the only player on the list who has a chance of returning to action against Jose Mourinho’s team. What Olmo’s absence means for Real Madrid Olmo is a crucial player for Hansi Flick and Barcelona, and Madrid would be glad to have one less headache to worry about. The Spain international offers Barça creativity between the lines, intelligent movement in midfield and the ability to turn games on their heads. Dani Olmo has performed very well forBarçaa in previous Clasicos. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Olmo has always tended to perform well in Clasicos since his return to Barça , and his absence is good news for Madrid. However, his replacement, Fermin Lopez, is equally potent and brings a different kind of energy for Madrid to contend with. Madrid will be looking to exploit any uncertainty in Barcelona’s line-up while attempting to close the six-point gap between the rivals. Nevertheless, Barcelona still possess enough attacking quality to cause serious problems, particularly through Lamine Yamal and their midfield combinations. Los Blancos need to play a perfect game to get the victory against Flick’s Barça on Sunday, and it remains to be seen how things pan out.

item.title: Barcelona injury news: Key midfielder facing four to five weeks out after recent injury vs PSG
item.description: Barcelona injury news: Key midfielder facing four to five weeks out after recent injury vs PSG Barcelona have suffered a potentially significant injury setback ahead of El Clasico, with Dani Olmo set to miss Sunday’s meeting with Real Madrid after being forced off against Paris Saint-Germain. According to a report from AS , the Spain international is unlikely to recover in time for the showdown at the weekend, leaving Hansi Flick facing another selection headache. The full extent of the injury remains unconfirmed, however, with further medical tests needed before Barcelona can establish a definitive recovery timeline. Dani Olmo injury raises fresh concerns for Barcelona Olmo was handed a starting place against PSG, with Flick choosing him ahead of Fermin Lopez in midfield. His evening was cut short in the 27th minute following a collision with PSG midfielder Vitinha. The Barcelona playmaker went to ground and quickly realised he could not continue, prompting him to request a substitution. Fermin subsequently replaced him, while television footage showed Olmo visibly distressed by the setback. Rather than heading straight to the dressing room, the injured midfielder remained on the bench after leaving the pitch. His reaction showed the disappointment of suffering a possible injury at such a crucial stage of Barcelona’s season. Initial reports suggest Olmo may have sustained a tear in his left adductor muscle. If that diagnosis is confirmed, the problem would be serious enough to rule him out of Sunday’s El Clasico and potentially several subsequent fixtures. MRI scan to determine Olmo’s El Clasico availability Right now, Barcelona are awaiting further clarity on the midfielder’s condition. According to AS, an MRI scan scheduled for Wednesday in Barcelona is expected to establish the diagnosis and provide a clearer indication of his recovery period. If the suspected muscle tear is confirmed, Olmo could face between four and five weeks on the sidelines. That would be a considerable blow for Flick, who would lose another strong option during a demanding run of fixtures. For now, his involvement against Real Madrid appears highly unlikely, and Flick is not expected to take unnecessary risks with an injured player, particularly when the medical assessment could reveal a problem requiring several weeks of rehabilitation. The final decision will depend on the scan results, but Barcelona must already prepare for the possibility of facing their fiercest rivals without the former RB Leipzig star. Flick faces selection headache before Real Madrid clash Olmo’s potential absence adds to Barcelona’s existing defensive concerns. Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia were already unavailable against Real Betis last Saturday, leaving Flick with additional issues to address ahead of El Clasico. Fermin’s introduction against PSG could strengthen his case for a midfield role, although Flick has other options available.

item.title: Celtics’ Mitchell Robinson shares injury update after tweaking ankle vs. Pistons
item.description: Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Celtics’ Mitchell Robinson shares injury update after tweaking ankle vs. Pistons appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Mitchell Robinson drew the start in his first official game for the Boston Celtics , their season-opener against the Detroit Pistons. In the second quarter of what would be a 121-113 loss, Robinson appeared to tweak his ankle on a battle for a loose ball. After Kevin Huerter missed a corner three, the Celtics center fought on the glass, but received a big bump from Pistons center Jalen Duren, and Robinson clearly twisted his ankle off the hardwood. Robinson writhed in pain on the ground for a few seconds as the Pistons capitalized on the five on four situation with a bonkers 360 layup from Ausar Thompson. Considering his history of ankle problems, this is a major injury concern for the Celtics. The good news is that Robinson stayed in the game and even suited up in the second half, and it doesn’t look as though the 28-year-old center will need to miss much time, if any, to recover from that scary moment. According to Gary Washburn of the Boston Globe, Robinson himself said that he’ll be “OK” moving forward. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This may have played a part in Robinson’s substandard outing in his official Celtics debut . He finished with just four points, and perhaps most glaringly, just three rebounds. He did block two shots, but he was a non-factor on the glass. This is something that Robinson aims to rectify. “I got my a** kicked on the glass. I can’t have no starts like that. It’s cool to get out there and put on that Boston jersey for the first time in a regular-season game, but overall, I still didn’t do what I needed to do. I gotta compete better. I feel like I didn’t compete at a high level that I normally do and I was kind of slow on a lot of things,” Robinson added. The Celtics’ slate is only about to get more difficult, as they will host the New York Knicks on Friday for their home opener. Related: Celtics’ Jayson Tatum admits shot ‘felt good’ despite woes vs. Pistons Related: Celtics’ Derrick White gets candid about Paul George’s 38-point eruption vs. Pistons

item.title: 'We were up to the challenge' - Goalscorer Desire Doue praises ruthless PSG after ending Barcelona's 11-game unbeaten run in Champions League classic
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-BARCELONA - AFP French starlet inspires Paris triumph Doue has praised Les Parisiens' clinical display after conquering their Spanish visitors to halt the La Liga leaders' 11-game unbeaten run in the Champions League. Building on his standout showing against Manchester City last week, the attacker broke the deadlock in the 38th minute with a low drive into the bottom corner. That opener arrived during a first half where the Blaugrana conceded 10 shots on target, their worst tally since at least 2003-04 . High-pressing hosts punish defensive errors High-pressing hosts punish defensive errors The hosts' aggressive press caused chaos after just 79 seconds when Khvicha Kvaratskhelia hit the post following a turnover by Pedri. Visiting goalkeeper Joan Garcia then denied Ousmane Dembele and twice thwarted substitute Ferran Torres after Dembele went off injured, while Russian stopper Matvey Safonov kept out Raphinha and Fermin Lopez at the other end. Reflecting on how his side rose to the occasion when speaking to PSG TV , Doue said: "We knew it was going to be a match of the highest standard. We were up to the challenge and showed some great football. We took our chances. The aim was to score more goals than them, because we knew they could score as well. They are a quality opponent, but we got the win and that's fantastic." Second-half blitz seals historic tally Nineteen-year-old full-back Xavi Espart levelled at the near post 10 minutes after the restart, only for Lucas Hernandez to restore the hosts' advantage with a towering header from a corner. Although Lamine Yamal skipped past Warren Zaire-Emery to make it 2-2, Vitinha chested down a clearance to volley home less than two minutes later before Fabian Ruiz converted Achraf Hakimi's low cross. Victory takes the holders to 14 goals after three fixtures, matching Arsenal's 2010-11 record while becoming the first side since Barcelona between September 2016 and March 2017 to net at least four times in three straight home games in the competition. Highlighting his team's ability to respond instantly whenever the visitors drew level, Doue added: "No matter what happens during the game, we try and stay focused every time. We know our qualities, we know we can score at any moment, whether that's immediately after conceding a goal, or straight after scoring one ourselves, we are able to stay focused on what we have to do and tonight we did it well." Spanish trip awaits group leaders Spanish trip awaits group leaders Claiming maximum points moves PSG onto nine points from their opening three league-phase fixtures. The French champions will next travel to Spain to take on Villarreal on Tuesday, November 3, though they must first assess the extent of Dembele's first-half injury. Meanwhile, Barcelona remain on six points and will look to bounce back when they welcome Aston Villa to Camp Nou on the same night.
item.content:encoded: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-BARCELONA - AFP French starlet inspires Paris triumph Doue has praised Les Parisiens' clinical display after conquering their Spanish visitors to halt the La Liga leaders' 11-game unbeaten run in the Champions League. Building on his standout showing against Manchester City last week, the attacker broke the deadlock in the 38th minute with a low drive into the bottom corner. That opener arrived during a first half where the Blaugrana conceded 10 shots on target, their worst tally since at least 2003-04 . High-pressing hosts punish defensive errors High-pressing hosts punish defensive errors The hosts' aggressive press caused chaos after just 79 seconds when Khvicha Kvaratskhelia hit the post following a turnover by Pedri. Visiting goalkeeper Joan Garcia then denied Ousmane Dembele and twice thwarted substitute Ferran Torres after Dembele went off injured, while Russian stopper Matvey Safonov kept out Raphinha and Fermin Lopez at the other end. Reflecting on how his side rose to the occasion when speaking to PSG TV , Doue said: "We knew it was going to be a match of the highest standard. We were up to the challenge and showed some great football. We took our chances. The aim was to score more goals than them, because we knew they could score as well. They are a quality opponent, but we got the win and that's fantastic." Second-half blitz seals historic tally Nineteen-year-old full-back Xavi Espart levelled at the near post 10 minutes after the restart, only for Lucas Hernandez to restore the hosts' advantage with a towering header from a corner. Although Lamine Yamal skipped past Warren Zaire-Emery to make it 2-2, Vitinha chested down a clearance to volley home less than two minutes later before Fabian Ruiz converted Achraf Hakimi's low cross. Victory takes the holders to 14 goals after three fixtures, matching Arsenal's 2010-11 record while becoming the first side since Barcelona between September 2016 and March 2017 to net at least four times in three straight home games in the competition. Highlighting his team's ability to respond instantly whenever the visitors drew level, Doue added: "No matter what happens during the game, we try and stay focused every time. We know our qualities, we know we can score at any moment, whether that's immediately after conceding a goal, or straight after scoring one ourselves, we are able to stay focused on what we have to do and tonight we did it well." Spanish trip awaits group leaders Spanish trip awaits group leaders Claiming maximum points moves PSG onto nine points from their opening three league-phase fixtures. The French champions will next travel to Spain to take on Villarreal on Tuesday, November 3, though they must first assess the extent of Dembele's first-half injury. Meanwhile, Barcelona remain on six points and will look to bounce back when they welcome Aston Villa to Camp Nou on the same night.

Daniels, who stepped into Tampa Bay’s starting lineup following Baker Mayfield’s injury, grew up idolizing Rodgers. The young quarterback even had a poster of the veteran star on his bedroom wall as a kid. After Sunday’s game, Rodgers made sure to give Daniels a moment he would remember for life. item.title: Oilers’ Evan Bouchard stuns Wild in OT with birthday game-winner
item.description: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Oilers’ Evan Bouchard stuns Wild in OT with birthday game-winner appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Connor McDavid is skating his way toward unprecedented territory in the early portion of the 2026 NHL campaign, and Leon Draisaitl is contending for the league lead in goals, but Evan Bouchard is making sure to seize his share of the spotlight on the Edmonton Oilers . The superbly skilled defenseman, who turned 27 years old on Tuesday, continues to wreak havoc on opposing squads. Although the aforementioned franchise pillars thrived versus the Minnesota Wild, it was Bouchard who was wearing the cape by night’s end. Facing a shootout after the Oilers lost a 3-1 lead in the third period, the birthday boy fired the puck into the net to break a 3-3 tie with 1:28 remaining in overtime. Bouchard decides to be generous on his day and gifts the boisterous crowd at Rogers Place a thrilling victory. HAPPY BIRTHDAY BOUCHARD!!! 🥳 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) No better way to mark the occasion than with the @Energizer overtime winner! pic.twitter.com/LjkZAz4Q0g — NHL (@NHL) October 21, 2026 Bouchard now has seven goals on the year and also tallied his 11th assist. Draisaitl lit the lamp at the end of the first period and beginning of the second, boosting his total to eight. McDavid recorded three assists, including one on the game-winner, and now has an eye-popping 20 through just nine games played. When this fabulous trio is in sync, the Oilers should be near-unbeatable. The standings seems to reflect as much so far. Edmonton (7-1-1, 15 points) is just one point behind the Vegas Golden Knights for first place in the Western Conference. Hopefully, the boys will have time to take out the clutch Evan Bouchard for a proper birthday celebration before they begin preparation for Thursday’s big clash with the reigning Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes. Related: Oilers’ Connor McDavid makes unbelievable NHL history in OT win vs. Wild Related: Oilers’ Connor McDavid shifts focus away from torrid offensive start ahead of Wild clash

item.title: Victor Wembanyama Caught in Spurs-Thunder Scuffle After Hard Foul
item.description: San Antonio's Victor Wembanyama is a generational player. Getty The San Antonio Spurs and Victor Wembanyama are now in the 2026-27 regular season. The Spurs are taking on the Oklahoma City Thunder at the Frost Bank Center on Tuesday night. This marks the first time the franchises have squared off since San Antonio’s game seven win in the Western Conference Finals in May. This is surely the most significant budding rivalry in the Western Conference at the moment. The scuffle that took place on Tuesday is further evidence of this. Wembanyama Part of Scuffle Between Spurs, Thunder Oklahoma City and San Antonio were in the midst of a competitive battle, with the former leading the latter 37-28 at the 9:21 mark of the second quarter. This is when a major inflection point of the game took place. Spurs guard De’Aaron Fox threw Thunder F Chet Homgren to the ground , which set off a chain reaction of events. The chain reaction included Wembanyama placing himself in the middle of the scuffle. This led to a tense confrontation with Thunder F Jaylin Williams . The result of this moment? A flagrant one foul on Fox, as well as technical fouls on Wembanyama, Williams, Jalen Williams, and Kenrich Williams . This moment seemingly lit a fire under the Thunder, as they went into halftime with a 65-44 lead. Follow what this moment could mean for the Spurs’ franchise player and this rivalry moving forward. San Antonio-Oklahoma City Rivalry Brewing Even More This moment seems to exceed the player-on-player rivalry between Wembanyama and Holmgren. These two teams truly have a distaste for one another. This is obviously understandable, as each are pining for supremacy in the West. However, moments such as this open the door for situations to escalate beyond the point of return. Follow for post-game comments from key members of the Spurs pertaining to the in-game scuffle. item.title: Thunder HC Mark Daigneault speaks up on defense that Victor Wembanyama couldn’t solve
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Thunder HC Mark Daigneault speaks up on defense that Victor Wembanyama couldn’t solve appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Oklahoma City Thunder HC Mark Daigneault praised the team’s collective defensive performance after holding San Antonio Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama to one field goal in Tuesday night’s 116-104 season-opening road victory. Wembanyama scored 12 points on 1-for-13 shooting, including 0-for-4 from deep, despite grabbing 13 rebounds and blocking six shots. The Thunder built a 21-point halftime lead before withstanding San Antonio’s second-half push. Thunder sideline reporter Nick Gallo took to X, formerly Twitter, to share Daigneault’s postgame remarks. Daigneault credited Oklahoma City’s defensive execution, offensive approach, and collective effort after the Thunder held off San Antonio’s second-half comeback. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “We were really, really good on that end tonight, and intentional on offense… Everybody was ready to play. Everybody contributed. It was a great collective effort for 48 minutes. We weathered the storm well and recentered when appropriate.” San Antonio shot 14-for-48 (29.2%) before halftime, with Wembanyama missing all seven first-half attempts. Oklahoma City led by as many as 26 and took a 65-44 advantage into the break. The Spurs rallied after intermission, but the Thunder held on for a 12-point road win. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led Oklahoma City with 32 points, while Jared McCain scored 20 and hit six of eight three-point attempts. Their contributions supported Daigneault’s assessment of his team’s offense. Tuesday’s opener renewed last season’s Western Conference finals matchup. The Spurs eliminated the Thunder in seven games, winning Game 7 by a 111-103 score on May 30. Daigneault did not identify a primary defender or detail the Thunder’s defensive coverage against Wembanyama . However, Oklahoma City’s collective effort helped secure a 116-104 season-opening victory over the same Spurs team that ended the Thunder’s season less than five months ago. Related: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama calls out issues that got Thunder ‘having fun’ Related: Thunder star SGA gets 100% real on simple approach that helped OKC rip Spurs apart

item.title: 3 Most Likely Colts Moves After Chris Ballard Firing
item.description: The Colts likely have more changes coming after Chris Ballard's firing. Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 12: Michael Carter #22 of the Arizona Cardinals runs against Deforest Buckner #99 of the Indianapolis Colts during the second half in the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Getty Changes are coming for the Indianapolis Colts amid the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. While Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has indicated that she’s all-in on the 2026 season, the 2-4 record and upcoming schedule merits doubt. The Colts have the Minnesota Vikings, Jacksonville Jaguars and Dallas Cowboys over the next three weeks, and that doesn’t bode well for a turnaround. Here’s a look at the most likely changes for the Colts and when and how it plays out. Colts Fire Defensive Coordinator Lou Anarumo There’s already speculation of Anarumo sitting on the hot seat, and it will get hotter in Week 7 if the Colts can’t slow down the Vikings. Minnesota has one of the more meager offenses in the league with quarterback Kyler Murray, so Irsay-Gordon could pull the plug if the Colts give up anything north of 24 points and lose to the Vikings. The Colts’ defense needs an immediate turnaround after dropping 27.3 points per game over six weeks, and last year’s unit in Anarumo wasn’t much better. Colts Do Fire Sale at the Trade Deadline Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA – OCTOBER 12: Michael Carter #22 of the Arizona Cardinals runs against Deforest Buckner #99 of the Indianapolis Colts during the second half in the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Indianapolis doing a fire sale at the trade deadline will happen if the team falls to the Vikings, Jaguars and Cowboys. Even if the Colts go 1-2 in those games, a fire sale seems inevitable. Backup quarterback Anthony Richardson will finally get traded since the team hasn’t stuck with him on the field since his rookie year in 2023. The Colts aren’t going to get major compensation for a failed first-round draft pick, so Indianapolis will go much bigger and bolder in the trade market to clear salary cap space and acquire draft picks and new talent. Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner seems like the most likely trade candidate of all, even ahead of Richardson. The Colts can bank on a good return by trading Buckner, who has four sacks this year, because he clearly has a more quality football left at age 32. He also indirectly expressed wanting out. “I’m sick and tired of the same song and dance every year,” Buckner told reporters after Sunday’s loss to the Tennessee Titans . He also indirectly expressed wanting out. “I’m sick and tired of the same song and dance every year,” Buckner told reporters after Sunday’s loss to the Tennessee Titans . Trading wide receiver Keenan Allen seems like a inevitable move, too. Allen is a quality wideout, but the Colts need money and future draft capital more than a pass-catcher at 2-7 or 3-6. Teams such as the San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Rams and New England Patriots are likely interested in receiver help amid injuries this season. The Colts might be able to get more than normal for Allen because of it. Indianapolis’ least-likely moves are offensive guard Quenton Nelson and running back Jonathan Taylor. Quality offensive linemen are hard to come by, and Taylor is in his prime. The Colts will need significant trade packages to justify either move. Colts Head Coach Shane Steichen Loses His Job Steichen seems like the final domino to fall, but that’s only if the Colts make it to 3-6 at the trade deadline with competitive showings in all three of the upcoming games. He had one winning season at the Colts head coach in 2023, and the team had a strong start last year before the December losing streak. That said, Steichen won’t keep his job unless the Colts make a serious turnaround as this season goes on, and he likely will need to make the playoffs in order to keep his job. item.title: Thunder rookie Aday Mara’s NBA debut gets an honest assessment from Mark Daigneault
item.description: Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images Thunder rookie Aday Mara’s NBA debut gets an honest assessment from Mark Daigneault appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Aday Mara did not play much in his NBA debut, but Mark Daigneault made it clear that the rookie’s minutes told only part of the story as the Oklahoma City Thunder beat the San Antonio Spurs 116-104 on Tuesday night at Frost Bank Center in a rematch of last season’s Western Conference Finals. Mara logged just 12 minutes off the bench, but the Thunder head coach came away impressed with what the 21-year-old gave his team. “It was a great impact. He had probably one of the stretches of the game that was critical,” Daigneault said. “He didn’t seem overwhelmed by the atmosphere of the game.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mark Daigneault on Aday Mara’s NBA debut: “I think he’s proven to be a very impactful player.” pic.twitter.com/xXWQVy0cI4 — Clemente Almanza (@CAlmanza1007) October 21, 2026 Mara finished with seven points on 3-of-4 shooting, two rebounds, an assist and a block. He also turned his ankle late in the first quarter shortly after checking in, but he returned after a break in play and appeared to walk it off. For Daigneault, the performance was a continuation of what he saw throughout the exhibition slate. “I’m not really surprised with how he’s performed in the preseason. I think he’s proven to be a very impactful player,” Daigneault said. “His minutes weren’t high tonight, but his impact was.” Mara gave Oklahoma City plenty of reasons for optimism before the regular season . The 7-foot-3 center opened the preseason by going 15-for-15 from the field across his first two games, then posted 17 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and six blocks against the Atlanta Hawks. The Thunder selected Mara with the 12th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft after he helped Michigan win the national championship. He averaged 12.1 points, 6.8 rebounds and 2.6 blocks last season and was named Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year. His debut also came under a cloud. Basket Zaragoza, the Spanish club Mara played for before college, claims he remains under contract and has threatened legal action . The Thunder said no clearance from the club was needed for him to play in the NBA. On the court, though, Mara has already earned his coach’s confidence. “I’m only going to trust him more after seeing how he performed in such a high-level game,” Daigneault said. The Thunder will look to stay unbeaten when they face the Denver Nuggets on Thursday. Aday Mara did not play much in his NBA debut, but Mark Daigneault made it clear that the rookie’s minutes told only part of the story as the Oklahoma City Thunder beat the San Antonio Spurs 116-104 on Tuesday night at Frost Bank Center in a rematch of last season’s Western Conference Finals. Mara logged just 12 minutes off the bench, but the Thunder head coach came away impressed with what the 21-year-old gave his team. “It was a great impact. He had probably one of the stretches of the game that was critical,” Daigneault said. “He didn’t seem overwhelmed by the atmosphere of the game.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mark Daigneault on Aday Mara’s NBA debut: “I think he’s proven to be a very impactful player.” pic.twitter.com/xXWQVy0cI4 — Clemente Almanza (@CAlmanza1007) October 21, 2026 Mara finished with seven points on 3-of-4 shooting, two rebounds, an assist and a block. He also turned his ankle late in the first quarter shortly after checking in, but he returned after a break in play and appeared to walk it off. For Daigneault, the performance was a continuation of what he saw throughout the exhibition slate. “I’m not really surprised with how he’s performed in the preseason. I think he’s proven to be a very impactful player,” Daigneault said. “His minutes weren’t high tonight, but his impact was.” Mara gave Oklahoma City plenty of reasons for optimism before the regular season . The 7-foot-3 center opened the preseason by going 15-for-15 from the field across his first two games, then posted 17 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and six blocks against the Atlanta Hawks. The Thunder selected Mara with the 12th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft after he helped Michigan win the national championship. He averaged 12.1 points, 6.8 rebounds and 2.6 blocks last season and was named Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year. His debut also came under a cloud. Basket Zaragoza, the Spanish club Mara played for before college, claims he remains under contract and has threatened legal action . The Thunder said no clearance from the club was needed for him to play in the NBA. On the court, though, Mara has already earned his coach’s confidence. “I’m only going to trust him more after seeing how he performed in such a high-level game,” Daigneault said. The Thunder will look to stay unbeaten when they face the Denver Nuggets on Thursday. item.title: Doué and Vitinha burn bright as brittle Barcelona come unstuck against PSG
item.description: Fire, noise, fury, a sense of empty energy. And across town, a football match too. Do any of these randomly pitched autumnal Champions League fixtures mean anything? Probably not when you’re Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona, and the only game in town is risk-free TV income and a semi-guaranteed place in the knockout stuff. But this was still a dazzling occasion at the Parc des Princes, where the champions of France and Spain played out a light, open, frictionless, exhibition-style game of football. PSG finished 4-2 winners, having been pegged back to 2-2 midway through the second half. But this was also a game where the score almost did not seem to matter, and where the only really hard message was the frailty of the Barcelona backline and PSG’s thrilling attacking energy in these midweek A-games. Continue reading...

item.title: Mac Allister double sparks Liverpool’s thrilling comeback win over Villarreal
item.description: Andoni Iraola and Iñigo Pérez parked a long and close friendship in the buildup to their first competitive confrontation as coaches. The old Athletic Bilbao teammates will have a humdinger of a Champions League contest to dissect once communications are restored. Liverpool, ignited by Rio Ngumoha, recovered from two goals down against Villarreal to maintain their 100% record plus their gathering momentum. Alexis Mac Allister struck twice, Florian Wirtz capped recent improvement with his first goal of the season while Liverpool were dreadful for the opening 30 minutes, transformed after the break and fretting in stoppage time after Tani Oluwaseyi had volleyed in a third for Villarreal. The game flipped on Sergi Cardona’s mistake and Ronald Araújo’s equaliser with the final touch of the first half. “We weren’t able to handle the emotion tonight,” conceded Villarreal coach Pérez. Continue reading...

item.title: Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK Athens
item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

Arteta admitted his players had to be better in attacking terms and the discussion over how they are able to get the job done has tracked them to Germany where they face Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday night. item.title: US under-17 women beat Samoa 17-0 for biggest win in World Cup history
item.description: Result is largest margin at any age level of a World Cup DiMaria is first to score six at Fifa finals since Haaland Tournament is in year two of expanded 24-team field The United States began their U-17 Women’s World Cup campaign on Monday with a record-setting 17-0 win over Samoa the biggest win at any age level in World Cup history. The result surpassed the previous record for margin at an 11-a-side World Cup, a 16-0 win by Morocco against New Caledonia in the 2025 U-17 men’s World Cup. Ten players scored for the US, and forward Maddie DiMaria led with six goals in Salé, Morocco. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.description: Female players including Carlinha and Tayla Carolina have spoken out against the far right, who they fear will harm the women’s game as well as wider society The day before the first round of Brazilian elections, the Estádio do Morumbi hosted the second leg of the Brazilian Women’s Championship final, in which São Paulo drew 1-1 with Corinthians to win 3-2 on aggregate and secure the Brasileirão Women’s title. It had been an incredible final but after the game the goalkeeper Carlinha used an interview to appeal to her fans: “Never again Bolsonaro in power,” she shouted to a record-breaking TV audience of 23 million people. item.description: Peta calls on club to never again use a live animal mascot ‘There’s no reason to drag a wild animal into a stadium’ A leading animal rights group has urged Crystal Palace to retire their American bald eagle mascot because, it says, the matchday experience can leave the bird “frightened, disoriented and panicked” and put spectators at risk. In a letter to Palace’s chief executive, Sharon Lacey, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) called on the club to end Phoenix’s appearances at Selhurst Park and commit never to use a live animal mascot again. item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Leaving England is scary but I’m here to win’: Charlie Cresswell on Ligue 1 life and his international dream
item.description: Young centre-back could not see a way forward at Leeds so moved to France. Now he’s preparing for the biggest game of his life against Juventus By Get French Football News “Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision,” says Charlie Cresswell. It is a decision that he never thought he would make. His father, Richard, made a career as a footballer in England; his brother, Alfie, was coming through Leeds’ academy; Charlie was on the fringes of their first team when the opportunity arose to join Toulouse in 2024. “That was the biggest decision I made in football,” he says. “I’ve been a Leeds fan since I was eight. I’d been at the club since I was 10, but, looking back, I was 20 years old with no games and I needed to get out and go play.” Continue reading...

item.title: Konsa bullish about Arsenal’s Champions League hopes as Bayern clash looms
item.description: Centre-back has settled right in at Arsenal and is looking ‘to win everything’, starting with Wednesday’s duel against Harry Kane For Ezri Konsa, it was just a wonderfully satisfying challenge. The Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap had stolen in behind him up the inside left channel on Sunday. There were 93 minutes gone, Arsenal were 1-0 up and it was now or never for Forest. Konsa decreed that it would be never, curving his covering run back, matching Delap for pace and stretching into the perfect block tackle. So, another win for Arsenal : their 10th in 11 matches this season. Another clean sheet. And for Konsa, a continuation of what has been a dreamlike couple of months. Do points-saving last-minute challenges mean more when the defender is actually a fan of the club, too? Basically, yes. Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One
item.description: Gary Caldwell, club captain in 2013 and now manager, needs much more than the weekend win against Reading to disperse the clouds If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern‑day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win against Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: FC Copenhagen Women have a ‘startup-like’ brand. Now they need results
item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch. The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. Now they are in the top division and “playing with the big dogs”, as their head of women’s football, Romaney Pinnock, coins it, and they must adapt to stay there. Continue reading...

item.title: My old teammate Miroslav Klose is bucking a trend in German coaching | Philipp Lahm
item.description: ‘Miro’, now in charge at Nürnberg, knows the value of consistency and identity in an era of tinkering coaches who did not play professionally You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season. Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018. I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. The only change came during their title defence in Budapest , where Gianluigi Donnarumma no longer featured in goal, Luis Enrique having parted ways with the Italian European champion. core players: about 70 to 85% each remaining regular starters: 50 to 60% each squad players: 40 to 45% each fringe squad places: sharing the remaining maximum of 20% Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City are suddenly box-office in age of charge-rage and mega defiance | Barney Ronay
item.description: This is by far the most interesting this club have ever been and they faced PSG, a kind of twin entity in all this as oil state glove puppets Another day, another note of unreality; another vivid and brilliant spectacle that feels as though it has been whipped together out of meringue and burnt sugar. Time flies when the world is closing in. Two weeks on, this was Manchester City’s first home game since the verdict dropped, the irrefutable body of evidence was refuted, and English football entered its state of ongoing whiplash. In the stadium this felt like watching someone dance while the world burns. This was a brilliant game pegged out around six goals , a collapse, a comeback, posts and bars struck, saved penalties, and a performance of state-of-the-art omni-football from this brilliantly high-grade Paris Saint-Germain team. Continue reading...

item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. Continue reading...

item.title: Have any footballers ended their career with more own goals than goals? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the earliest trophyless seasons, scoring off one’s backside (part II) and the origins of ‘shithousery’ Mail us with all of your questions and answers “How many professional players have ended their senior careers with more own goals than goals for their own team?” wonders Peter Clark. In the past we’ve looked at the players with the most own goals , but we haven’t looked at those who ended their professional career in debit. “Southampton cult hero Francis Benali scored only one ‘positive’ goal in his career and was legendary for banging in goal-of-the-month contenders at his own end, most notably a bullet header against Oldham in the 1993-94 season ,” writes Daz Pearce. We could only find a couple of OGs for Benali, the other being against Manchester United in 1999-2000 . But we were unable to find a comprehensive Southampton database, so there’s a chance we’ve missed some beauties. Continue reading...

item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: Sliding Doors meets Biff’s Almanac: City saga stirs up a world of alternate histories | Max Rushden
item.description: Even New Romantics have a view but this long story will not be cut short amid endless hypotheticals and split narratives It’s Wednesday afternoon (UK time) and I find myself interviewing Tony Hadley on TalkSport about his upcoming big band tour. We play a bit of Spandau Ballet, chat about the classics and his career – hanging out with Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. In as much as you can deduce in a 10-minute chat on Zoom, Tony seems like an absolute gent. We do always try to bring it back to sport – Tony is an Arsenal fan, there’s a bit of Arteta, Leeds at the weekend. Tony brings up Billy Bremner and suggests that my co-host Charlie Baker and I are too young to remember him playing. We are, and how wonderful to be called young. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
